rules.rule_name: Skip Row Selection Validation When Prior Input Errors Exist
rules.rule_description: When account or card filter validation has already failed before row selection validation begins, the system bypasses all row selection checks entirely to avoid redundant or misleading error messages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prior Input Errors Exist? → Yes - Errors Already Exist → Skip Row Validation Exit

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Card List screen and either the Account ID filter or the Card Number filter has already been flagged as invalid (INPUT-ERROR is active)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to perform row selection validation on the 7 card selection fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system immediately skips all row selection validation steps and exits the validation routine without evaluating any of the 7 row selection codes, leaving all row-level error indicators unchanged

rules.rule_name: Count Total Row Selections Across All Seven Card Rows
rules.rule_description: Before evaluating individual row selections, the system counts the total number of action codes entered across all 7 card rows to determine whether the user has attempted to act on more than one card simultaneously.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Count Total Selections - Tally all S and U entries across all 7 card rows

acceptance_criteria.Given: No prior input errors exist and the system is proceeding with row selection validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system inspects the combined selection flags field (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS) which concatenates all 7 row selection entries
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system tallies the total count of all occurrences of 'S' (View) and 'U' (Update) values across all 7 row selection fields and stores the total count in the counter variable I for use in the multiple-selection check

rules.rule_name: Reject Submission When More Than One Card Row Is Selected
rules.rule_description: A user is only permitted to act on one card at a time. If the user enters a selection code ('S' or 'U') in more than one row simultaneously, the system rejects the submission and marks every selected row as being in error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: More Than One Row Selected? → Yes - Multiple Rows Selected → Set Multiple Selection Error - Mark all selected rows with error indicators

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has counted the total number of 'S' and 'U' entries across all 7 card rows and the total count is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The multiple-selection count check is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the overall input status to error (INPUT-ERROR), activates the multiple-selection error flag (WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION), copies the combined selection flags into the error flags field (WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS), and replaces every 'S' and 'U' in the error flags with '1' and every other character with '0', thereby marking exactly those rows that contained a selection code as rows in error

rules.rule_name: Initialize Selected Row Index Before Row-by-Row Evaluation
rules.rule_description: Before iterating through the 7 card rows to identify which row the user selected, the system resets the selected row index to zero to ensure no stale value from a prior screen interaction is carried forward.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Selected Row Index to Zero - Prepare to identify the single valid selection

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed the multiple-selection count check (regardless of whether a multiple-selection error was found or not) and is about to begin row-by-row evaluation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initializes the selected row tracking variable
acceptance_criteria.Then: The selected row index variable (I-SELECTED) is set to zero, indicating that no row has yet been identified as the user's intended selection

rules.rule_name: Record the Index of a Valid Single Row Selection
rules.rule_description: When a card row contains a valid action code ('S' for View or 'U' for Update), the system records that row's position number so that the subsequent action (navigate to Card Detail or Card Update) can be directed to the correct card.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Valid Code S or U - Record this row index as the selected row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is iterating through card rows 1 to 7 and the current row's selection field contains either 'S' (View) or 'U' (Update), which are the only two valid action codes
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection code for the current row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current row number (1 through 7) into the selected row index variable (I-SELECTED), making it available for the downstream action routing logic to determine which card's Account Number and Card Number to pass to the next screen

rules.rule_name: Mark a Valid Selection Row as Error When Multiple Selections Were Made
rules.rule_description: Even though a row contains a technically valid action code ('S' or 'U'), if the user selected more than one row simultaneously, each individually valid selection must also be flagged as an error to visually indicate to the user which rows caused the conflict.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Multiple Selection Error Active? → Yes - Multiple Selection Error → Mark This Row with Error Indicator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is iterating through card rows 1 to 7, the current row contains a valid selection code ('S' or 'U'), and the multiple-selection error flag (WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION) is active
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether a multiple-selection error is in effect for this valid row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the row-level error indicator for the current row (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR(I)) to '1', causing that row's selection field to be highlighted in red on the screen to alert the user that this row is part of an invalid multiple-selection

rules.rule_name: Accept Blank Row Selection as No Action Required
rules.rule_description: A card row where the user has left the selection field blank or empty is considered a deliberate non-selection and requires no validation action. The system silently skips such rows.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Blank Entry - No Action Required - Skip this row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is iterating through card rows 1 to 7 and the current row's selection field is blank (SELECT-BLANK condition is true, meaning the field contains spaces or low-values)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection code for the current row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system takes no action for that row, does not set any error indicator, does not update the selected row index, and proceeds to evaluate the next row

rules.rule_name: Reject and Flag an Invalid Action Code Entered in a Card Row
rules.rule_description: If a user enters any value other than 'S', 'U', or blank in a card row's selection field, the system treats it as an unrecognized action code, marks that row as invalid, and sets an error message to inform the user of the correct valid values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Invalid Code Entered - Mark This Row with Error Indicator - Set Invalid Action Code Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is iterating through card rows 1 to 7 and the current row's selection field contains a value that is neither 'S' (View), 'U' (Update), nor blank
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection code for the current row and finds it does not match any valid code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the overall input status to error (INPUT-ERROR), sets the row-level error indicator for the current row (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR(I)) to '1' to trigger red highlighting on that row's selection field, and if no prior error message has been set, activates the invalid action code error message (WS-INVALID-ACTION-CODE) to inform the user that only 'S' or 'U' are accepted selection values

sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:

    C{More than one\nrow selected?}
    D[Mark session as\nInput Error state]
    E[Flag as Multiple\nSelections Error]
    F[Copy current selection flags\nto error tracking area]
    G[Mark all rows that had S or U\nwith error indicator '1'\nMark all other rows with '0']
    H([Continue to\nIndividual Row Validation])
    I([Continue to\nIndividual Row Validation])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Yes - Multiple Rows Selected| D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    C -->|No - Single or No Selection| I

rules.rule_name: Count Total Row Selections Across Card List
rules.rule_description: When a user submits the card list screen, the system scans all 7 row selection fields simultaneously and tallies the total number of View ('S') and Update ('U') action codes entered across all rows to determine how many rows have been selected.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Scan all 7 rows and count total number of S and U action codes entered

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the card list screen with one or more selection fields filled in across up to 7 card rows, and no prior account or card filter validation errors exist
acceptance_criteria.When: The system scans the combined selection flag area (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS) representing all 7 row selection fields and counts every occurrence of 'S' (View action) and every occurrence of 'U' (Update action) to produce a total selection count
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system holds the total count of all 'S' and 'U' entries found across all 7 rows in counter variable I, which is then used to determine whether a single or multiple row selection has been made

rules.rule_name: Detect Multiple Row Selections and Set Error State
rules.rule_description: The card list screen enforces a business rule that only one card row may be actioned at a time. If a user enters action codes in more than one row, the system must immediately flag the entire submission as invalid and record the specific nature of the error as a multiple-selection violation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: More than one row selected? → Mark session as Input Error state → Flag as Multiple Selections Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed counting all 'S' (View) and 'U' (Update) entries across all 7 card list rows and the total count is held in counter I
acceptance_criteria.When: The total count of selected rows (I) is greater than 1, meaning the user has entered action codes in more than one row simultaneously
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the overall input validation state to INPUT-ERROR (marking the entire screen submission as invalid) and sets the WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION flag to TRUE to specifically identify this as a multiple-selection error, distinguishing it from other types of row selection errors

rules.rule_name: Capture Selection State for Error Row Identification
rules.rule_description: When a multiple-selection error is detected, the system must preserve a snapshot of which rows were selected so that each individual row can be independently evaluated and marked with an error indicator. This snapshot is copied into a dedicated error tracking area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Copy current selection flags to error tracking area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that more than one row has been selected (INPUT-ERROR is TRUE and WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system copies the current combined selection flags (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS, containing the raw 'S', 'U', or blank values for all 7 rows) into the error tracking flags area (WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error tracking area (WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS) holds an exact copy of the user's selection entries, ready to be transformed into per-row error indicators in the next step

rules.rule_name: Mark Each Selected Row with Error Indicator for Display
rules.rule_description: After a multiple-selection error is detected, the system must identify precisely which rows the user selected so they can be highlighted in red on the screen. Every row that had a View ('S') or Update ('U') code is marked with error indicator '1', and all other rows are marked with '0' to clearly distinguish erroneous selections from non-selected rows.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark all rows that had S or U with error indicator '1' Mark all other rows with '0'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error tracking area (WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS) contains a copy of the user's row selection entries, with 'S', 'U', or blank values for each of the 7 rows, and a multiple-selection error has been confirmed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the error tracking area by replacing every 'S' character with '1', every 'U' character with '1', and every remaining character (blanks or any other value) with '0'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error tracking area (WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS) contains a binary error map where '1' indicates a row that was incorrectly selected as part of a multiple-selection violation and '0' indicates a row that was not selected, enabling the screen to highlight all offending rows in red during the subsequent display step

rules.rule_name: Skip Row Selection Validation When Prior Input Errors Exist
rules.rule_description: When input errors have already been detected during account or card filter validation, the row selection validation is bypassed entirely to avoid cascading error messages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prior Input Errors Exist?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Card List screen and prior input validation errors have already been flagged (INPUT-ERROR is TRUE) due to invalid account filter or card number filter entries
acceptance_criteria.When: The row selection validation routine (2250-EDIT-ARRAY) is invoked
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system skips all row selection validation checks entirely and exits the routine immediately without evaluating any of the 7 row selection fields, preserving the existing error state

rules.rule_name: Count Total Row Selections Across All Seven Rows
rules.rule_description: Before validating individual row selections, the system tallies the total number of View ('S') and Update ('U') action codes entered across all 7 card list rows to determine if multiple rows have been selected.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Count Total Selections - Tally all S and U codes across all 7 rows

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Card List screen with no prior input errors, and the 7 row selection fields (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS, positions 1-7) may contain any combination of 'S', 'U', or other values
acceptance_criteria.When: The row selection validation routine begins counting selections
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system inspects the combined selection flags string (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS) and tallies the total count (stored in counter variable I) of all occurrences of 'S' (View) and 'U' (Update) codes across all 7 rows, treating both 'S' and 'U' as valid selection indicators for the purpose of counting

rules.rule_name: Flag Multiple Row Selection Error When More Than One Row Is Selected
rules.rule_description: A user is only permitted to select one card row per screen submission. If more than one row has been marked with a View or Update action code, the system flags an error and identifies all offending rows for visual highlighting.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: More Than 1 Row Selected?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Card List screen and the total count of 'S' and 'U' selections across all 7 rows is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The multiple-selection check is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets INPUT-ERROR to TRUE, sets the WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION flag to TRUE, copies the selection flags into WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS, and replaces every 'S' and 'U' in WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS with '1' (error indicator) and all other characters with '0', so that every row that had a selection is individually marked for red highlighting on the screen

rules.rule_name: Initialize Selected Row Index Before Row-by-Row Evaluation
rules.rule_description: Before iterating through the 7 card rows to identify which row was selected, the system resets the selected row index to zero to ensure no stale selection index from a prior screen interaction is carried forward.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Row Counter - Start examining Row 1 of 7

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to begin the row-by-row evaluation loop for all 7 card list rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The row iteration is initialized
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the selected row index (I-SELECTED) to zero, then begins iterating from row 1 through row 7 incrementing by 1 for each iteration

rules.rule_name: Record Selected Row Index for Valid View or Update Selection
rules.rule_description: When a row contains a recognized action code ('S' for View or 'U' for Update), the system records that row's position as the selected row so it can be used to navigate to the appropriate detail or update screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Valid Code S or U - Record this row index as the selected row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is evaluating a specific row (row number I, where I is between 1 and 7) and the row's selection field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(I)) contains either 'S' (View) or 'U' (Update), satisfying the SELECT-OK condition
acceptance_criteria.When: The row selection code is evaluated as valid
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current row number (I) into the selected row index variable (I-SELECTED) for later use in navigating to the Card Detail or Card Update screen

rules.rule_name: Mark Valid Selected Row with Error Indicator When Multiple Selections Detected
rules.rule_description: When a valid selection code exists on a row but the multiple-selection error is active (more than one row was selected), the system marks that row with an error indicator so it is highlighted in red on the screen to alert the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Multiple Selection Error Active? - Mark This Row with Error Indicator for Red Highlighting

acceptance_criteria.Given: A row contains a valid selection code ('S' or 'U') and the multiple-selection error flag (WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION) is TRUE, indicating that more than one row was selected in the same submission
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes that valid-but-conflicting row selection
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the row-level error indicator (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR(I)) to '1' for that specific row, which will cause the selection field to be displayed in red on the screen

rules.rule_name: Accept Blank Row Selection as No Action Requested
rules.rule_description: A blank selection field on a card row is a valid state indicating the user has not requested any action for that card. No error is raised and the row is simply skipped.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Blank Selection - No action taken for this row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is evaluating a specific row (row number I, where I is between 1 and 7) and the row's selection field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(I)) is blank or empty, satisfying the SELECT-BLANK condition
acceptance_criteria.When: The row selection code is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system takes no action for that row, does not set any error indicators, does not update I-SELECTED, and continues to the next row

rules.rule_name: Flag Invalid Action Code and Mark Row with Error Indicator
rules.rule_description: When a row's selection field contains a value that is neither a recognized action code ('S' or 'U') nor blank, the system treats it as an invalid action code, marks the row for error highlighting, and sets the overall input error state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Invalid Action Code - Mark row with Error Indicator '1'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is evaluating a specific row (row number I, where I is between 1 and 7) and the row's selection field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(I)) contains a value that is not 'S', not 'U', and not blank (the OTHER condition in the EVALUATE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The row selection code is evaluated as unrecognized
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and sets the row-level error indicator (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR(I)) to '1' for that specific row, which will cause the selection field to be displayed in red on the screen

rules.rule_name: Set Invalid Action Code Error Message When No Prior Message Exists
rules.rule_description: When an invalid action code is detected in a row selection field, the system sets a user-facing error message only if no prior error message has already been set, preserving the first error message encountered during the validation pass.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Error Message Slot Available? - Set Message: Invalid Action Code Entered by User

acceptance_criteria.Given: An invalid action code has been detected in a row selection field (INPUT-ERROR is TRUE for that row) and the error message slot is currently empty (WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF is TRUE, meaning no prior error message has been set during this validation pass)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to set the invalid action code error message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error message (WS-ERROR-MSG) to indicate that an invalid action code was entered by the user (WS-INVALID-ACTION-CODE is set to TRUE, which populates WS-ERROR-MSG with the invalid action code message); if a prior error message already exists (WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF is FALSE), the existing message is preserved and no new message is written

rules.rule_name: Identify Valid Row Selection Action Code
rules.rule_description: For each card row displayed on the Card List screen, the system evaluates whether the user-entered selection code represents a recognized action. Only 'S' (View card detail) and 'U' (Update card) are valid action codes. This determination drives all subsequent row-level processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is entered code valid action? S = View or U = Update

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card row is displayed on the Card List screen and the user has entered a value in the row's selection field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the entered selection code for row I during input validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the entered code matches a valid action code — 'S' for View or 'U' for Update — the row is treated as a valid selection and proceeds to be recorded as the selected row; otherwise the system checks whether the field is blank or contains an unrecognized code

rules.rule_name: Record the Selected Card Row
rules.rule_description: When a user enters a valid action code ('S' or 'U') in a card row's selection field, the system records the row index as the currently selected row. This selected row index is later used to retrieve the corresponding account number and card number for navigation to the Card Detail or Card Update screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark this row as the Selected Row

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card row on the Card List screen contains a valid selection code of 'S' (View) or 'U' (Update)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system validates the row selection during input processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current row number (I) as the selected row index (I-SELECTED), making the account number and card number of that row available for subsequent navigation to the Card Detail or Card Update screen

rules.rule_name: Apply Error Indicator to Valid Selection When Multiple Selections Detected
rules.rule_description: Even when a row contains a valid action code ('S' or 'U'), if the system has already detected that more than one row was selected in the same submission, the valid row must also be flagged with an error indicator. This enforces the single-selection-per-submission policy by visually highlighting all selected rows in red, including those with individually valid codes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Multiple Selection Error Active? / Apply Error Indicator to this Row Highlight in Red

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card row contains a valid selection code of 'S' or 'U', and the system has detected that more than one row was selected in the current submission (Multiple Selection Error is active)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the valid selection code for row I
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system applies an error indicator ('1') to the row's selection error flag (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR for row I), causing the selection field to be highlighted in red on the screen to indicate the multiple-selection violation

rules.rule_name: Allow Valid Single Selection to Proceed Without Error
rules.rule_description: When a card row contains a valid action code ('S' or 'U') and no multiple-selection error has been detected, the row is accepted as a clean, valid selection. No error indicator is applied, and the selection is available for use in navigating to the Card Detail or Card Update screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row is Valid Selection - Proceed

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card row contains a valid selection code of 'S' (View) or 'U' (Update), and no multiple-selection error is active for the current submission
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes validation of the row selection code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row is accepted as a valid single selection with no error indicator applied, the row index is retained as the selected row, and the system proceeds without setting any error condition for this row

rules.rule_name: Skip Blank Row Selection — No Action Required
rules.rule_description: When a user leaves a card row's selection field completely blank (spaces or low-values), it means the user has made no selection for that row. The system treats this as a deliberate non-selection and skips the row entirely without raising any error or recording it as a selected row.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is entered code completely Blank? No selection made / Skip this Row No action required

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card row is displayed on the Card List screen and the user has left the row's selection field blank (empty, spaces, or low-values)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection code for that row during input validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system skips the row without recording it as a selected row, without applying any error indicator, and without setting any error message — processing continues to the next row

rules.rule_name: Flag Unrecognized Selection Code as Input Error
rules.rule_description: When a user enters a value in a card row's selection field that is neither a valid action code ('S' or 'U') nor blank, the system treats it as an invalid input. The overall input is flagged as being in error, and the specific row is marked with an error indicator so it can be highlighted in red on the screen to draw the user's attention.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Row as Input Error / Apply Error Indicator to this Row Highlight in Red

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card row on the Card List screen contains a selection field value that is not 'S', not 'U', and not blank
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection code for that row during input validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the overall input status to error (INPUT-ERROR), applies an error indicator ('1') to the row's selection error flag (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR for row I) causing the selection field to be highlighted in red, and proceeds to check whether an error message needs to be set

rules.rule_name: Set Invalid Action Code Error Message on First Occurrence
rules.rule_description: When an unrecognized selection code is detected in a card row, the system must display an error message to inform the user. However, to preserve the first error message encountered during validation (error message priority rule), the system only sets the 'Invalid Action Code' message if no prior error message has already been established during the current validation pass.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is there already an Error Message set? / Set Error Message: Invalid Action Code Entered

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card row has been identified as containing an unrecognized selection code (not 'S', 'U', or blank), and the system is determining whether to set an error message
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether an error message has already been set during the current input validation pass (WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF flag is active, meaning no prior message exists)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If no prior error message exists, the system sets the error message to indicate an invalid action code was entered (WS-INVALID-ACTION-CODE); if an error message was already set by a prior validation rule (account filter or card filter error), the existing message is preserved and no new message is written

rules.rule_name: Clear Screen Rows and Initialize Page State Before Forward Read
rules.rule_description: Before reading card records forward, all display rows must be cleared and the row counter reset to zero so that stale data from a previous page is not shown to the user. The next-page indicator is optimistically set to 'exists' at the start.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear all 7 screen rows
Set screen row counter to zero
Set Next Page Exists indicator

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward card read operation is about to begin for a new page of results
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initializes the forward read process
acceptance_criteria.Then: All 7 card display rows are cleared to empty values, the screen row counter is set to zero, and the Next Page Exists indicator is set to true in preparation for reading

rules.rule_name: Position Card File Browse at or After Starting Card Number
rules.rule_description: The card file browse must be positioned at the record whose card number is greater than or equal to the provided starting card number key, ensuring the forward read begins at the correct position in the file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Start browsing Card File
from given starting Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: A starting card number key (WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM) has been set for the forward read
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates a browse of the Card File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The file browse is positioned at the first card record whose card number is greater than or equal to the starting card number key, so that subsequent reads proceed forward from that position

rules.rule_name: Read Next Card Record Sequentially from Card File
rules.rule_description: During the forward browse loop, the system reads the next sequential card record from the Card File. The outcome determines whether a valid record was found, the end of file was reached, or another condition occurred.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read Next Card Record
from Card File

acceptance_criteria.Given: A browse of the Card File has been started and the read loop is active
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the next card record sequentially from the Card File
acceptance_criteria.Then: A card record containing Card Number, Account ID, and Active Status is retrieved; if the end of the file is reached, the end-of-file condition is flagged; if a normal or duplicate record response is received, the record is available for filter evaluation

rules.rule_name: Filter Card Records by Account ID When Account Filter Is Active
rules.rule_description: When a user has supplied a valid Account ID as a filter, only card records whose Account ID exactly matches the filter value should be included in the display. Records with a non-matching Account ID are excluded and the next record is read.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Does Record Pass
Account ID Filter?
If filter active, account
must match

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully read from the Card File and an Account ID filter has been validated and is active
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the card record's Account ID matches the Account ID filter value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card record's Account ID equals the filter Account ID, the record passes the account filter and proceeds to card number filter evaluation; if the card record's Account ID does not match, the record is excluded from the display and the system reads the next record without incrementing the row counter

rules.rule_name: Filter Card Records by Card Number When Card Number Filter Is Active
rules.rule_description: When a user has supplied a valid Card Number as a filter, only card records whose Card Number exactly matches the filter value should be included in the display. Records with a non-matching Card Number are excluded and the next record is read.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Does Record Pass
Card Number Filter?
If filter active, card number
must match

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has passed the Account ID filter check and a Card Number filter has been validated and is active
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the card record's Card Number matches the Card Number filter value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card record's Card Number equals the filter Card Number, the record passes the card number filter and is included in the display; if the card record's Card Number does not match, the record is excluded from the display and the system reads the next record without incrementing the row counter

rules.rule_name: Store Qualifying Card Record Data in Screen Display Row
rules.rule_description: Each card record that passes all active filters is stored in the next available screen display row. The row counter is incremented to track how many qualifying records have been collected for the current page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Store Card Number,
Account ID, Active Status
in next screen row
Increment row counter

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has passed all active filter checks (Account ID filter and Card Number filter)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the qualifying card record in the display list
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card's Card Number, Account ID, and Active Status are stored in the next available screen row position (indexed by the row counter), and the row counter is incremented by 1

rules.rule_name: Save First Qualifying Card as Page-Up Navigation Bookmark
rules.rule_description: The first qualifying card record on a page must be saved as the navigation bookmark so that the system can navigate back to the beginning of this page when the user presses PF7 (page up). If the page number has not yet been set, it is initialized to 1.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is this the
First Qualifying
Record?
Save Card Number as
First Card Key for
Page Up navigation
Set Page Number if not set

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has just been stored as the first qualifying record on the current page (row counter equals 1)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system identifies this as the first qualifying record for the page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card's Account ID is saved as the First Card Account ID bookmark and the card's Card Number is saved as the First Card Number bookmark for page-up navigation; additionally, if the current screen page number is zero, it is incremented by 1 to set the page number to 1

rules.rule_name: Stop Reading When Page Is Full and Save Last Card Navigation Bookmark
rules.rule_description: When 7 qualifying card records have been collected, the current page is full. The system saves the last card's details as the navigation bookmark for page-down (PF8) navigation and stops the read loop to proceed with checking for additional records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Have 7 Rows
been filled?
Save current Card Number
as Last Card Key for
Page Down navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: Card records are being read and stored in screen display rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The row counter reaches the maximum of 7 rows (WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The read loop is flagged to exit, and the current card's Account ID and Card Number are saved as the Last Card Account ID and Last Card Number bookmarks respectively, to be used as the starting position for the next page-down navigation

rules.rule_name: Peek Ahead to Determine If a Next Page of Records Exists
rules.rule_description: After filling a full page of 7 records, the system reads one additional record to determine whether more records exist beyond the current page. This controls whether the PF8 (next page) navigation option is available to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read one more record
to check if next page exists
Additional Record
Found?
Update Last Card Key
to this additional record
Set NEXT PAGE EXISTS indicator

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current page has been filled with 7 qualifying card records and the last card bookmark has been saved
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads one additional record from the Card File beyond the last displayed record
acceptance_criteria.Then: If an additional record is found (normal or duplicate response), the Next Page Exists indicator is set to true and the Last Card Account ID and Last Card Number bookmarks are updated to this additional record's values; if the end of file is reached, the Next Page Not Exists indicator is set to true and the message 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW' is set (only if no prior error message exists)

rules.rule_name: Handle End of Card File During Forward Read
rules.rule_description: When the end of the card file is reached during the main forward read loop (before filling 7 rows), the system marks that no next page exists, saves the last read card details as the Last Card bookmark, and sets an informational message for the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set NO MORE PAGES indicator
Save last read Card Number
as Last Card Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is reading card records in the forward read loop and has not yet filled all 7 display rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The end of the Card File is reached (no more records to read)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The read loop is flagged to exit, the Next Page Not Exists indicator is set to true, the last read card's Account ID and Card Number are saved as the Last Card Account ID and Last Card Number bookmarks, and the message 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW' is set if no prior error message has already been set

rules.rule_name: Set No Records Found Indicator When First Page Returns Zero Results
rules.rule_description: When the system is on the first page of results and the end of file is reached without finding any qualifying records, a specific 'No Records Found' indicator is set to inform the user that no cards match the applied filters.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is this the First Page
AND zero records found?
Set NO RECORDS FOUND
message for user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The end of the Card File has been reached during a forward read
acceptance_criteria.When: The current screen page number is 1 (first page) AND the screen row counter is zero (no qualifying records were found)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The No Records Found indicator is set to true, which will suppress normal informational messages and display a 'no records found' notification to the user

rules.rule_name: End Card File Browse After Forward Read Completes
rules.rule_description: After the forward read loop has completed (either by filling 7 rows, reaching end of file, or encountering an error), the card file browse session must be formally closed to release file resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Stop browsing Card File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward card read loop has completed for any reason (page full, end of file, or error)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the forward read operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Card File browse session is ended, releasing the file browse position and completing the forward read process

key_functionalities.title: Next Page Existence Check
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Next Page Existence Check])
    B{Has a Full Page of\n7 Records Been Filled?}
    C[Record the Last Card Key\nof the Current Page\nAccount ID and Card Number]
    D[Attempt to Read\nOne More Record\nBeyond Current Page]
    E{Was Another\nRecord Found?}
    F[Update Last Card Key\nwith the Peeked Record's\nAccount ID and Card Number]
    G[Mark: Next Page EXISTS\nUser Can Press Page Down\nto See More Records]
    H[Mark: Next Page DOES NOT EXIST\nUser is Viewing the\nLast Available Page]
    I([End: Next Page Indicator Updated])
    J{Page Not Yet Full\nLess Than 7 Records}
    K([Continue Reading\nCurrent Page Records])
    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Page is Full| C
    B -->|No - Page Not Full| J
    J --> K
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E -->|Yes - More Records Exist| F
    F --> G
    E -->|No - End of File Reached| H
    G --> I
    H --> I

rules.rule_name: Detect When a Full Page of Card Records Has Been Filled
rules.rule_description: After each card record is added to the display list during a forward read, the system checks whether the maximum number of records per page (7) has been reached to determine if a next-page existence check should be triggered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Has a Full Page of 7 Records Been Filled?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is reading card records forward from the card file and adding qualifying records to the current page display list
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of records added to the current page display equals the maximum allowed records per page (7)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system stops adding records to the current page, records the last card's Account ID and Card Number as the Last Card Key bookmark for the current page, and proceeds to perform a peek-ahead read to determine if more records exist beyond the current page

rules.rule_name: Record the Last Card Key of the Current Page Before Peek-Ahead
rules.rule_description: Before attempting to read beyond the current page, the system saves the Account ID and Card Number of the last record displayed on the current page. These values serve as navigation bookmarks enabling forward and backward pagination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record the Last Card Key of the Current Page Account ID and Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current page has been filled with exactly 7 card records and the system is about to check whether more records exist
acceptance_criteria.When: The page-full condition is confirmed (record count equals 7)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system saves the Account ID of the 7th (last) card record into the Last Card Account ID bookmark (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-ACCT-ID) and saves the Card Number of the 7th (last) card record into the Last Card Number bookmark (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-NUM), so that these values can be used as the starting point for the next page navigation

rules.rule_name: Attempt to Read One Additional Record Beyond the Current Page
rules.rule_description: After filling a full page of 7 records and recording the last card key, the system performs a single additional sequential read from the card file to determine whether any records exist beyond the current page, without displaying that record to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Read One More Record Beyond Current Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current page has been filled with 7 card records and the Last Card Key bookmark has been recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a peek-ahead read by attempting to read the next sequential record from the card file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system evaluates the outcome of this read attempt — either a record is found (indicating more pages exist) or the end of the card file is reached (indicating the current page is the last page) — and updates the next-page indicator accordingly

rules.rule_name: Mark Next Page as Existing and Update Last Card Key When More Records Are Found
rules.rule_description: When the peek-ahead read successfully retrieves a record beyond the current page, the system confirms that a next page is available for navigation and updates the Last Card Key bookmark with the peeked record's details to ensure accurate forward navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update Last Card Key with the Peeked Record's Account ID and Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a peek-ahead read after filling the current page with 7 records
acceptance_criteria.When: The peek-ahead read returns a valid card record (read is successful — normal or duplicate record response)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the next-page indicator as 'Next Page EXISTS' (enabling the Page Down / PF8 navigation option for the user), and updates the Last Card Account ID bookmark with the peeked record's Account ID and updates the Last Card Number bookmark with the peeked record's Card Number

rules.rule_name: Mark Next Page as Not Existing When End of Card File Is Reached
rules.rule_description: When the peek-ahead read reaches the end of the card file, the system confirms that the user is viewing the last available page of card records and sets an informational message to notify the user that no further records are available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark: Next Page DOES NOT EXIST User is Viewing the Last Available Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a peek-ahead read after filling the current page with 7 records
acceptance_criteria.When: The peek-ahead read reaches the end of the card file (no more records exist beyond the current page)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the next-page indicator as 'Next Page DOES NOT EXIST' (disabling the Page Down / PF8 navigation option), and if no prior error message has already been set, displays the informational message 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW' to inform the user that the current page is the last available page

rules.rule_name: Continue Reading Records When Current Page Is Not Yet Full
rules.rule_description: While the number of qualifying card records added to the current page display is less than the maximum of 7, the system continues reading the next sequential record from the card file without triggering the next-page existence check.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Page Not Yet Full Less Than 7 Records

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is in the forward read loop and is adding qualifying card records to the current page display list
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of records added to the current page is less than the maximum records per page (fewer than 7 records)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does not trigger the next-page existence check, does not record the Last Card Key bookmark, and continues reading the next sequential record from the card file to attempt to fill the remaining slots on the current page

key_functionalities.title: Backward Card Record Reading
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Page Up Navigation\nBackward Card Record Reading])
    B[Clear All Screen Rows\nPrepare for fresh page data]
    C[Save Current First Card Key\nas Backward Browse Starting Point]
    D[Open Backward Browse\non Card File from\nCurrent First Card Key]
    E[Set Screen Position Counter\nto Bottom of Screen\nRow 8 - fills upward to Row 1]
    F[Skip First Record Read\nThis is current page's\nfirst record - not needed]
    G[Read Previous Card Record\nfrom Card File]
    H{Record Read\nSuccessful?}
    I[27:Apply Account and\nCard Number Filters\nDoes record match search criteria?]
    J{Record Passes\nAll Filters?}
    K[Place Record Data in\nCurrent Screen Row:\nAccount Number, Card Number,\nCard Active Status]
    L[Move Screen Position\nUp One Row]
    M{Screen Position\nReached Row 1?\n7 Records Filled?}
    N[Update First Card Key\nto This Record's Card Number\nThis becomes new page start]
    O{More Records\nto Read?}
    P[Close Card File Browse]
    Q([End: Previous Page\nReady for Display])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H -->|Yes - Record Available| I
    H -->|No - Beginning of File\nor Error| P
    I --> J
    J -->|No - Excluded by Filter| G
    J -->|Yes - Include Record| K
    K --> L
    L --> M
    M -->|No - Need More Records| O
    O -->|Yes - Continue Reading| G
    O -->|No - No More Records| P
    M -->|Yes - Page Full\n7 Records Collected| N
    N --> P
    P --> Q

rules.rule_name: Clear Screen Rows Before Backward Page Load
rules.rule_description: Before reading the previous page of card records, all existing screen display rows must be cleared to ensure no stale data from the prior page remains visible to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear All Screen Rows
Prepare for fresh page data

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has requested to navigate to the previous page of the card list
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward card record reading process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: All 7 screen display rows (Account Number, Card Number, Card Active Status, and Selection fields) are cleared to empty/low values before any new records are loaded

rules.rule_name: Save Current First Card Key as Backward Browse Starting Point
rules.rule_description: The card number of the first record currently displayed on screen must be saved and used as the starting position for the backward file browse, ensuring the system navigates backward from the correct position in the card file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Current First Card Key
as Backward Browse Starting Point

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current page is displaying card records and the first card key (WS-CA-FIRST-CARDKEY) is known
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward card record reading process begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current first card key is copied to the last card key field (WS-CA-LAST-CARDKEY) and used as the starting position (RIDFLD) for opening the backward browse on the card file

rules.rule_name: Open Backward Browse on Card File from First Card Key
rules.rule_description: The card file browse must be opened at or after the current page's first card key position using a greater-than-or-equal (GTEQ) positioning, enabling subsequent backward reads to retrieve the preceding page of records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Open Backward Browse
on Card File from
Current First Card Key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward browse starting point has been set to the current page's first card key
acceptance_criteria.When: The card file browse is opened for backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card file browse is started at the position of the current first card key using GTEQ positioning, so that backward reads will retrieve records preceding the current page

rules.rule_name: Initialize Screen Position Counter to Bottom of Screen for Upward Fill
rules.rule_description: Because records are read in reverse order (newest-to-oldest), the screen array must be filled from the bottom row upward. The screen position counter is initialized to one position beyond the maximum screen lines (7+1=8) so that after the first skip-read decrement it starts at row 7 and fills upward to row 1.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Screen Position Counter
to Bottom of Screen
Row 8 - fills upward to Row 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card file backward browse has been successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen position counter is initialized for backward page filling
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen position counter (WS-SCRN-COUNTER) is set to WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES + 1 (value of 8), so that after skipping the first record and decrementing, the first qualifying record is placed in the bottom-most display row (row 7) and subsequent records fill upward toward row 1

rules.rule_name: Skip First Record Read to Exclude Current Page's First Record
rules.rule_description: The first backward read after opening the browse returns the current page's first record, which is already displayed and should not be included in the previous page. This record must be skipped, and the screen position counter decremented to align with the correct starting row.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Skip First Record Read
This is current page's
first record - not needed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward browse has been opened at the current page's first card key position
acceptance_criteria.When: The first backward read is performed immediately after opening the browse
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the read is successful (NORMAL or DUPREC response), the screen position counter is decremented by 1 (from 8 to 7) and the record data is discarded — this record is the current page's first record and must not appear on the previous page. If the read fails with any other response, the backward reading process is terminated with an error.

rules.rule_name: Read Previous Card Record from Card File in Backward Direction
rules.rule_description: Each iteration of the backward read loop retrieves the next preceding card record from the card file, moving backward through the file to populate the previous page of the card list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read Previous Card Record
from Card File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward browse is open and the screen position counter is greater than 0
acceptance_criteria.When: A backward read is performed in the read loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads the previous card record from the card file into the CARD-RECORD area, capturing Card Number, Account ID, and Card Active Status for potential display

rules.rule_name: Handle Unsuccessful Backward Record Read
rules.rule_description: When a backward read returns an unexpected result (not a normal read or duplicate record), the backward reading loop must be terminated to prevent further processing on an invalid file state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record Read
Successful?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A backward read has been performed on the card file
acceptance_criteria.When: The read response is anything other than NORMAL or DUPREC (e.g., beginning of file or file error)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The read loop is immediately exited, the operation name 'READ' and the card file name are recorded in the error context fields, and the file error message is set in WS-ERROR-MSG for display to the user

rules.rule_name: Apply Account Number Filter During Backward Read
rules.rule_description: When an account number filter has been entered by the user, each card record read during backward navigation must be checked to ensure its account ID matches the filter value. Records belonging to a different account must be excluded from the display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
27:Apply Account and
Card Number Filters
Does record match search criteria?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A backward card record read has returned a valid record AND an account number filter is active (FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The account filter check is applied to the retrieved card record
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card record's Account ID (CARD-ACCT-ID) matches the filter Account ID (CC-ACCT-ID), the record is retained for potential display. If the card record's Account ID does NOT match the filter Account ID, the record is excluded and the next record is read without placing this record on the screen

rules.rule_name: Apply Card Number Filter During Backward Read
rules.rule_description: When a card number filter has been entered by the user, each card record read during backward navigation must be checked to ensure its card number matches the filter value. Records with a different card number must be excluded from the display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
27:Apply Account and
Card Number Filters
Does record match search criteria?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A backward card record read has returned a valid record AND a card number filter is active (FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The card number filter check is applied to the retrieved card record
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card record's Card Number (CARD-NUM) matches the filter Card Number (CC-CARD-NUM-N), the record is retained for potential display. If the card record's Card Number does NOT match the filter Card Number, the record is excluded and the next record is read without placing this record on the screen

rules.rule_name: Apply Combined Account and Card Number Filters During Backward Read
rules.rule_description: When both an account number filter and a card number filter are active simultaneously, a card record must satisfy BOTH filter conditions to be included in the display. Failing either filter results in the record being excluded.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
27:Apply Account and
Card Number Filters
Does record match search criteria?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A backward card record read has returned a valid record AND both an account number filter (FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID) and a card number filter (FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID) are active
acceptance_criteria.When: Both filters are applied sequentially to the retrieved card record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The record is included in the display only if CARD-ACCT-ID matches CC-ACCT-ID AND CARD-NUM matches CC-CARD-NUM-N. If either condition fails, the record is excluded and the system reads the next record

rules.rule_name: Place Qualifying Record in Current Screen Row During Backward Fill
rules.rule_description: Each card record that passes all active filters is placed into the current screen row position, storing the Account Number, Card Number, and Card Active Status for display to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Place Record Data in
Current Screen Row:
Account Number, Card Number,
Card Active Status

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been read successfully and has passed all active filter checks (account and/or card number filters)
acceptance_criteria.When: The record is accepted for display on the previous page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card's Card Number (CARD-NUM) is stored in WS-ROW-CARD-NUM at the current screen counter position, the card's Account ID (CARD-ACCT-ID) is stored in WS-ROW-ACCTNO at the current screen counter position, and the card's Active Status (CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS) is stored in WS-ROW-CARD-STATUS at the current screen counter position

rules.rule_name: Move Screen Position Up One Row After Placing Record
rules.rule_description: After placing a qualifying record into the current screen row, the screen position counter must be decremented by 1 to move the fill position upward toward row 1, maintaining the correct top-to-bottom display order for records that were read in reverse.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Move Screen Position
Up One Row

acceptance_criteria.Given: A qualifying card record has been successfully placed into the current screen row (WS-SCRN-COUNTER position)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen row placement is complete
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen position counter (WS-SCRN-COUNTER) is decremented by 1, moving the next available fill position one row upward on the screen

rules.rule_name: Detect When Previous Page is Fully Populated with 7 Records
rules.rule_description: After each record is placed and the screen position counter is decremented, the system must check whether all 7 screen rows have been filled. When the counter reaches 0, the previous page is complete and the read loop must stop.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Screen Position
Reached Row 1?
7 Records Filled?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A qualifying card record has been placed in a screen row and the screen position counter has been decremented
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen position counter (WS-SCRN-COUNTER) is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If WS-SCRN-COUNTER equals 0, all 7 screen rows have been filled — the read loop is flagged to exit (READ-LOOP-EXIT set to TRUE) and the first card key bookmark is updated. If WS-SCRN-COUNTER is greater than 0, the loop continues reading the next previous record

rules.rule_name: Update First Card Key Bookmark to New Page's First Record
rules.rule_description: When the previous page has been fully populated with 7 records, the card number and account ID of the last record placed (which is the topmost record on the new page) must be saved as the new first card key bookmark. This bookmark is used for future navigation — both for further backward navigation and for re-reading this page forward.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Update First Card Key
to This Record's Card Number
This becomes new page start

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen position counter has reached 0, indicating all 7 rows of the previous page have been filled
acceptance_criteria.When: The read loop exit condition is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID of the current card record (CARD-ACCT-ID) is saved to WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-ACCT-ID and the Card Number of the current card record (CARD-NUM) is saved to WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM, establishing this record as the new starting point for the now-displayed previous page

rules.rule_name: Close Card File Browse After Backward Read Completion
rules.rule_description: After the backward read loop has completed — whether because 7 records were collected, no more records exist, or an error occurred — the card file browse must be closed to release file resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Card File Browse

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward card record reading loop has ended for any reason (page full, beginning of file reached, or error encountered)
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward read process concludes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card file browse is closed (ENDBR issued on the card file), and the previous page data is ready for screen display

key_functionalities.title: Record Filter Application
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Evaluate Card Record])
    B[Default Decision:\nMark Record as INCLUDE]
    C{Is Account\nFilter Active?}
    D{Does Card's Account ID\nMatch the Account Filter?}
    E[EXCLUDE Record:\nAccount ID Does Not Match]
    F{Is Card Number\nFilter Active?}
    G{Does Card Number\nMatch the Card Number Filter?}
    H[EXCLUDE Record:\nCard Number Does Not Match]
    I([Record INCLUDED:\nPasses All Active Filters])
    J([Record EXCLUDED:\nDoes Not Meet Filter Criteria])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Yes - Account Filter is Set| D
    C -->|No - No Account Filter Applied| F
    D -->|Yes - Account ID Matches| F
    D -->|No - Account ID Does Not Match| E
    E --> J
    F -->|Yes - Card Number Filter is Set| G
    F -->|No - No Card Number Filter Applied| I
    G -->|Yes - Card Number Matches| I
    G -->|No - Card Number Does Not Match| H
    H --> J

rules.rule_name: Default Record Inclusion Before Filter Evaluation
rules.rule_description: Before any filter criteria are evaluated, every card record retrieved during a browse operation is initially marked as eligible for display. This default-include stance ensures that records are only excluded when a specific active filter condition explicitly disqualifies them.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Default Decision:
Mark Record as INCLUDE

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved from the card file during a forward or backward browse operation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins evaluating whether the record should be displayed on the card list screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The record is marked as INCLUDED by default, meaning it is considered eligible for display unless a subsequent active filter condition explicitly excludes it

rules.rule_name: Account Filter Active Status Determination
rules.rule_description: The system determines whether an account filter has been applied by the user. An account filter is considered active only when the user has entered a valid numeric Account ID in the account filter field on the card list screen. If no account filter is active, the account ID of the card record is not evaluated and the record proceeds to the card number filter check.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Account
Filter Active?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been retrieved and marked as INCLUDED by default, and the user may or may not have entered an Account ID in the account filter field on the card list screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the account filter flag is set to valid (indicating the user supplied a valid numeric Account ID as a filter)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the account filter is active (flag is valid), the system proceeds to compare the card record's Account ID against the filter value; if the account filter is not active, the system skips the account ID comparison and proceeds directly to evaluate the card number filter

rules.rule_name: Account ID Match Evaluation and Exclusion
rules.rule_description: When an account filter is active, the system compares the account ID on the card record against the account ID entered by the user as a filter. If the values do not match, the record is immediately excluded from the display list and no further filter checks are performed for that record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Does Card's Account ID
Match the Account Filter?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account filter is active with a valid numeric Account ID entered by the user, and a card record has been retrieved from the card file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the card record's Account ID field against the user-supplied Account ID filter value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card record's Account ID exactly matches the filter value, the record remains INCLUDED and the system proceeds to evaluate the card number filter; if the card record's Account ID does not match the filter value, the record is immediately marked as EXCLUDED and no further filter evaluation is performed for that record

rules.rule_name: Card Number Filter Active Status Determination
rules.rule_description: The system determines whether a card number filter has been applied by the user. A card number filter is considered active only when the user has entered a valid numeric Card Number in the card number filter field on the card list screen. If no card number filter is active, the card number of the record is not evaluated and the record is confirmed as included for display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Card Number
Filter Active?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has passed the account filter check (or no account filter was active) and is still marked as INCLUDED, and the user may or may not have entered a Card Number in the card number filter field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the card number filter flag is set to valid (indicating the user supplied a valid numeric Card Number as a filter)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card number filter is active (flag is valid), the system proceeds to compare the card record's Card Number against the filter value; if the card number filter is not active, the record is confirmed as INCLUDED and passes all filter checks, making it eligible for display on the card list screen

rules.rule_name: Card Number Match Evaluation and Exclusion
rules.rule_description: When a card number filter is active, the system compares the card number on the card record against the card number entered by the user as a filter. If the values do not match, the record is immediately excluded from the display list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Does Card Number
Match the Card Number Filter?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card number filter is active with a valid numeric Card Number entered by the user, and a card record has already passed the account filter check and is still marked as INCLUDED
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the card record's Card Number field against the user-supplied Card Number filter value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card record's Card Number exactly matches the filter value, the record is confirmed as INCLUDED and passes all active filter checks, making it eligible for display on the card list screen; if the card record's Card Number does not match the filter value, the record is immediately marked as EXCLUDED and is not displayed on the card list screen

rules.rule_name: Combined Filter Logic - Record Must Pass All Active Filters
rules.rule_description: A card record is eligible for display on the card list screen only when it satisfies all active filter conditions simultaneously. Both the account filter and the card number filter operate as AND conditions — a record must match every active filter to be included. Records that fail any single active filter are excluded from display regardless of other filter results.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record INCLUDED:
Passes All Active Filters

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been retrieved from the card file during browsing, and one or both of the following filters may be active: an Account ID filter and/or a Card Number filter entered by the user on the card list screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the card record against all active filters sequentially — first the account filter (if active), then the card number filter (if active)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The record is marked as INCLUDED and displayed on the card list screen only if it passes every active filter check (Account ID matches when account filter is active AND Card Number matches when card number filter is active); if the record fails any single active filter, it is marked as EXCLUDED and is not displayed on the card list screen, with no further filter evaluation performed for that record

key_functionalities.title: Session State Persistence
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Session State Persistence Begins])
    B[Record Current Program Identity
Save current transaction ID,
program name, map name,
and mapset name into session context]
    C[Save Application-Wide Session Data
Copy the application-wide communication area
into the combined session storage area
as the first part of the saved state]
    D[Save Program-Specific Session Data
Copy this program's specific data
card keys, screen number, pagination indicators,
and return flags into the second part
of the combined session storage area]
    E[Combine Both Areas into One
Merge application-wide data and
program-specific data into a single
combined communication area
ready for handoff to CICS]
    F[Return Control to CICS
Pass the combined communication area
back to CICS so all session state
is preserved for the next
screen interaction]
    G([Session State Saved Successfully])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program Identity Before Session Handoff
rules.rule_description: Before returning control to CICS, the Card List program must stamp the session context with its own identity — including the transaction ID, program name, current map name, and current mapset name — so that the next screen interaction knows which program last handled the session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record Current Program Identity
Save current transaction ID,
program name, map name,
and mapset name into session context

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card List program has completed processing a user interaction (any key press or action) and is preparing to return control to CICS to await the next user input
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reaches the session state persistence step (COMMON-RETURN) prior to issuing the CICS RETURN command
acceptance_criteria.Then: The session context must be updated with: (1) the current transaction ID saved as the 'from transaction ID' field in the application-wide communication area (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), (2) the current program name saved as the 'from program' field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), (3) the current mapset name saved as the 'last mapset' field (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), and (4) the current map name saved as the 'last map' field (CDEMO-LAST-MAP), so that the next program or screen interaction can identify the originating program and map

rules.rule_name: Save Application-Wide Session Data as First Part of Combined Storage
rules.rule_description: The application-wide communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which holds shared session data such as user type, account ID, card number, program entry state, and navigation context, must be copied into the first portion of the combined session storage area (WS-COMMAREA) before returning to CICS.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Application-Wide Session Data
Copy the application-wide communication area
into the combined session storage area
as the first part of the saved state

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card List program has completed processing and the application-wide communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) contains the current session's shared data including user type, account ID, card number, program entry/re-entry state, last map, last mapset, and next program routing information
acceptance_criteria.When: The program executes the session state save step in COMMON-RETURN
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entire contents of the application-wide communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be copied verbatim into the beginning (first part) of the combined session storage area (WS-COMMAREA), occupying positions 1 through the full length of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, preserving all shared session fields for use by subsequent programs

rules.rule_name: Save Program-Specific Session Data as Second Part of Combined Storage
rules.rule_description: The Card List program's own session data (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), which includes card key bookmarks for pagination (first and last card numbers and account IDs), the current screen/page number, pagination state indicators (first page flag, next page exists flag, last page shown flag), and program return flags, must be saved into the second portion of the combined session storage area immediately after the application-wide data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Program-Specific Session Data
Copy this program's specific data
card keys, screen number, pagination indicators,
and return flags into the second part
of the combined session storage area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card List program has completed processing and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA contains the program-specific session state including: the first card number bookmark (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM), the last card number bookmark (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-NUM), the first card account ID bookmark (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-ACCT-ID), the last card account ID bookmark (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-ACCT-ID), the current screen/page number (WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM), pagination indicators (CA-FIRST-PAGE, CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS/NOT-EXISTS, CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN/NOT-SHOWN), and program return flags
acceptance_criteria.When: The program executes the session state save step in COMMON-RETURN after the application-wide data has been placed in WS-COMMAREA
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entire contents of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA must be copied into WS-COMMAREA starting at the position immediately after the end of the application-wide communication area (at offset: LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1) and extending for the full length of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, so that all card list pagination state and navigation bookmarks are preserved for the next screen interaction

rules.rule_name: Merge Application-Wide and Program-Specific Data into Single Combined Communication Area
rules.rule_description: The combined session storage area (WS-COMMAREA) must be constructed as a single contiguous block by placing the application-wide communication area in the first segment and the program-specific communication area in the second segment, with no gap between them, forming one unified communication area ready to be passed to CICS.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Combine Both Areas into One
Merge application-wide data and
program-specific data into a single
combined communication area
ready for handoff to CICS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The application-wide communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) both contain current, up-to-date session state data after all processing for the current user interaction is complete
acceptance_criteria.When: The program constructs the combined communication area in COMMON-RETURN
acceptance_criteria.Then: The combined session storage area (WS-COMMAREA) must be structured as: Segment 1 — positions 1 to LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA contain the full application-wide communication area data; Segment 2 — positions (LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1) to (LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + LENGTH OF WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) contain the full program-specific communication area data; the two segments must be contiguous with no padding or gap between them, forming a single unified block whose total length equals the sum of both individual area lengths

rules.rule_name: Return Control to CICS with Preserved Session State
rules.rule_description: After all session state has been saved into the combined communication area, the Card List program must return control to CICS specifying the same transaction ID so that the next user interaction (key press) will re-invoke this same program, and passing the full combined communication area so all session state is available when the program is next entered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Return Control to CICS
Pass the combined communication area
back to CICS so all session state
is preserved for the next
screen interaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) has been fully populated with both the application-wide session data and the program-specific session data (card keys, screen number, pagination indicators, return flags), and the program identity fields (transaction ID, program name, map, mapset) have been recorded in the session context
acceptance_criteria.When: The program issues the CICS RETURN command in COMMON-RETURN
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control must be returned to CICS with: (1) the next transaction ID set to the current program's own transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID), ensuring the same Card List transaction is re-invoked on the next user key press, (2) the combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) passed as the COMMAREA, and (3) the length of the COMMAREA set to the full length of WS-COMMAREA, so that the complete session state — including pagination bookmarks, page number, filter values, and navigation flags — is available when the program is next entered

key_functionalities.title: No Records Found Notification
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Forward Read Completed])
    B{Was this the\nFirst Page?\nScreen Number = 1}
    C{Were any qualifying\nrecords found?\nRecord Count = 0}
    D[Set 'No Records Found' Indicator\nFlag that no credit cards match\nthe current search criteria]
    E{Is No Records\nFound Flag Set?}
    F[Suppress Action Instructions\nDo not show 'TYPE S FOR DETAIL,\nU TO UPDATE' message]
    G[Display 'No Records Found'\nMessage to User\nNo credit cards match\ncurrent search criteria]
    H[Normal Page Display\nShow records with\naction instructions]
    I([End: Screen Displayed to User])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - First Page| C
    B -->|No - Not First Page| H
    C -->|Yes - Zero Records Found| D
    C -->|No - Records Were Found| H
    D --> E
    E -->|Yes| F
    F --> G
    G --> I
    H --> I

rules.rule_name: Detect No Matching Credit Cards on First Page Search
rules.rule_description: When the system performs a forward read of credit card records and reaches the end of the card file on the very first page without finding any qualifying records, it must set a 'No Records Found' indicator to signal that no credit cards match the current search criteria (account ID filter and/or card number filter).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set 'No Records Found' Indicator
