Flag that no credit cards match
the current search criteria

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward read of the credit card file has been performed, the current page being displayed is Page 1 (screen number equals 1), and the system has reached the end of the card file
acceptance_criteria.When: The count of qualifying records found on this page is zero (no records passed the account ID and/or card number filters)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Records Found' indicator to TRUE, signaling that no credit cards match the current search criteria entered by the user

rules.rule_name: Suppress Action Instructions When No Records Found
rules.rule_description: When the 'No Records Found' indicator is active, the system must suppress the standard informational action instructions message (which normally guides users to type 'S' for card detail or 'U' to update a card). Showing action instructions when there are no records to act upon would be misleading to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Suppress Action Instructions
Do not show 'TYPE S FOR DETAIL,
U TO UPDATE' message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing the card list screen for display and has completed reading card records from the file
acceptance_criteria.When: The 'No Records Found' indicator is set to TRUE (meaning zero qualifying credit card records were found matching the search criteria)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does NOT display the informational action instructions message (the message guiding users to type 'S' for detail or 'U' to update) on the screen, leaving the informational message area blank

rules.rule_name: Display No Records Found Message to User
rules.rule_description: When the card file read completes on the first page with zero qualifying records, the system must communicate to the user that no credit cards match their current search criteria. The 'No More Records To Show' message is set as the error message, and the action instructions are suppressed, resulting in a screen that clearly indicates no matching records exist.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display 'No Records Found'
Message to User
No credit cards match
current search criteria

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a forward read of the credit card file, the current page is Page 1, the end of the card file has been reached, and no qualifying records were found (record count equals zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The 'No Records Found' indicator is TRUE and no prior error message has been set (error message flag is in the OFF/blank state)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error message to 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW', sets the 'No Records Found' indicator, suppresses the informational action instructions message, and displays the card list screen to the user with the error message visible and no card data rows populated

rules.rule_name: Bypass No Records Check When Not on First Page
rules.rule_description: The 'No Records Found' indicator is only evaluated and set when the system is reading the very first page of results. If the system is reading any page other than the first page, the no-records check is not applicable, and the screen proceeds with normal display including action instructions for any records shown.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Normal Page Display
Show records with
action instructions

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a forward read of the credit card file and has reached the end of the card file
acceptance_criteria.When: The current screen number is NOT equal to 1 (the user is on a page beyond the first page of results)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does NOT set the 'No Records Found' indicator regardless of the record count, and the screen is displayed normally with any found records and the standard informational action instructions message visible

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user launches the Credit Card List screen with no prior session context (communication area length is zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects no existing session data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system initializes all working storage and communication areas to empty values, sets the transaction ID to the current transaction, sets the program name to the current program, sets the user type to standard user, sets the program state to 'entering', sets the current map and mapset identifiers, sets the page position to FIRST PAGE, and sets the last page indicator to NOT YET SHOWN

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Time Program Entry Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user accesses the Credit Card List screen for the very first time with no prior session context, the system initializes all working areas and sets the session to start from the first page of card records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user returns to the Credit Card List screen and a prior session context exists (communication area length is greater than zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects existing session data in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system restores the full CARDDEMO communication area from the saved session data, and restores the program-specific communication area (containing first card key, last card key, current screen number, and pagination state indicators) from the saved session data starting at the offset after the main communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session Context Restoration on Return
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user returns to the Credit Card List screen from a prior interaction, the system restores all previously saved session data including pagination bookmarks and screen state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program state is set to 'entering' AND the originating program is not the Credit Card List program itself
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects it is being entered fresh from a different program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets the program-specific communication area to empty values, sets the program state to 'entering', sets the current map to the card list map, sets the page position to FIRST PAGE, and sets the last page indicator to NOT YET SHOWN

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fresh Start Detection When Entering from Another Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Credit Card List screen is entered fresh from a different program, all local pagination and session context is reset to ensure a clean starting state regardless of any prior state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user presses any key on the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the pressed key against the list of valid keys
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the key is ENTER, PF3, PF7, or PF8, it is marked as a valid key and processed accordingly; if the key is any other key (PF1, PF2, PF4, PF5, PF6, PF9-PF12, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, or any other), the key is marked as invalid and the system defaults the action to ENTER key processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Function Key Validation and Defaulting
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system recognizes only specific function keys as valid actions on the Credit Card List screen. Any unrecognized key press is treated as the ENTER key to ensure predictable behavior.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card List screen and the session originated from this program (FROM-PROGRAM equals this program)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the transaction ID to the current transaction, sets the originating program to the current program, sets the user type to standard user, sets the program state to 'entering', sets the last mapset and map to the current card list mapset and map, sets the destination program to the main menu program (COMEN01C), sets the next mapset to the menu mapset, sets the next map to the current card list map, sets the exit message indicator, and transfers control via XCTL to the main menu program (COMEN01C) passing the current communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Exit to Main Menu via PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses PF3 while on the Credit Card List screen, the system immediately transfers control to the main menu program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user presses a key on the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed is NOT PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the last page indicator to NOT YET SHOWN, ensuring the 'no more pages' message logic is reset for the current interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Pagination Last-Page State Reset on Non-PF8 Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any key other than PF8 is pressed, the system resets the last-page-shown indicator to prevent stale pagination state from persisting across interactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Input validation has detected one or more errors (INPUT-ERROR is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the error condition in the main action routing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the current error message to the screen error message field, sets the originating program to the current program, sets the last mapset and map to the current card list mapset and map, sets the next program, mapset, and map to the current card list values; AND if the account filter is NOT in error AND the card number filter is NOT in error, the system performs a forward read of card records starting from the first card key bookmark; then the system sends the screen with all error indicators and returns to CICS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Input Error Handling with Conditional Forward Read and Re-display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When input validation errors exist, the system sets appropriate error context and conditionally reads card records if the filter fields themselves are valid, then re-displays the screen with error indicators.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is viewing the Credit Card List screen and is currently on the first page (CA-FIRST-PAGE is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 (page up)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the first card key bookmark to the card record ID field, performs a forward read of card records starting from that key, and sends the screen; the message setup logic will display 'NO PREVIOUS PAGES TO DISPLAY' because PF7 was pressed on the first page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Page Up Navigation When Already on First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to navigate to a previous page while already on the first page, the system informs the user and re-displays the current first page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is viewing the Credit Card List screen and a next page of records exists (CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 (page down)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the last card key bookmark (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-NUM) to the card record ID field, increments the screen number by 1, performs a forward read of up to 7 card records starting from that key applying active filters, and sends the updated screen displaying the next page of card records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Page Down Navigation to Next Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user navigates forward and more records exist beyond the current page, the system advances the page counter and reads the next set of card records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is viewing the Credit Card List screen and is NOT on the first page (CA-FIRST-PAGE is false)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 (page up)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the first card key bookmark (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM) to the card record ID field, decrements the screen number by 1, performs a backward read of up to 7 card records by: copying the first card key to the last card key, positioning the file at or after that key, reading one record backward to skip the current boundary record, then reading backward filling display rows from position 7 down to position 1 applying active filters, updating the first card key bookmark to the first record found, and sends the updated screen displaying the previous page of card records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Page Up Navigation to Previous Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user navigates backward and is not on the first page, the system decrements the page counter and reads the previous set of card records by browsing backward through the card file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card List screen, the session originated from this program (FROM-PROGRAM equals this program), and exactly one row has 'S' entered in its selection field (VIEW-REQUESTED-ON is true for row I-SELECTED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the transaction ID to the current transaction, sets the originating program to the current program, sets the user type to standard user, sets the program state to 'entering', sets the last mapset and map to the current card list values, sets the next program to the Card Detail program (COCRDSLC), sets the next mapset to the card detail mapset, sets the next map to the card detail map, moves the account number from the selected row (WS-ROW-ACCTNO at I-SELECTED) to the CDEMO account ID, moves the card number from the selected row (WS-ROW-CARD-NUM at I-SELECTED) to the CDEMO card number, and transfers control via XCTL to the Card Detail program (COCRDSLC) passing the current communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer to Card Detail View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects a card row for viewing by entering 'S', the system transfers control to the Card Detail program passing the selected card's account and card number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card List screen, the session originated from this program (FROM-PROGRAM equals this program), and exactly one row has 'U' entered in its selection field (UPDATE-REQUESTED-ON is true for row I-SELECTED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the transaction ID to the current transaction, sets the originating program to the current program, sets the user type to standard user, sets the program state to 'entering', sets the last mapset and map to the current card list values, sets the next program to the Card Update program (COCRDUPC), sets the next mapset to the card update mapset, sets the next map to the card update map, moves the account number from the selected row (WS-ROW-ACCTNO at I-SELECTED) to the CDEMO account ID, moves the card number from the selected row (WS-ROW-CARD-NUM at I-SELECTED) to the CDEMO card number, and transfers control via XCTL to the Card Update program (COCRDUPC) passing the current communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer to Card Update Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects a card row for updating by entering 'U', the system transfers control to the Card Update program passing the selected card's account and card number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card List screen and the action does not match any of the specific handled conditions (not an input error, not PF7 on first page, not PF8 with next page, not PF7 not on first page, not ENTER with S selection, not ENTER with U selection)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reaches the OTHER/default branch of the main action routing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the first card key bookmark (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM) to the card record ID field, performs a forward read of card records starting from that key applying active filters, and sends the screen displaying the current page of card records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Forward Read and Display for Unhandled Conditions
all_rules.Rule_Description: For any condition not explicitly handled by the main action routing, the system performs a forward read from the first card key bookmark and re-displays the current page as a safe default behavior.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Screen header initialization is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the screen output area to low values, retrieves the current system date and time, populates the first title line with the application title (CCDA-TITLE01), populates the second title line with the screen title (CCDA-TITLE02), sets the transaction name field to the current transaction ID, sets the program name field to the current program name, formats and sets the current date in MM/DD/YY format, formats and sets the current time in HH:MM:SS format, sets the page number field to the current screen number (WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM), and initializes the informational message field with the current info message in dark red color

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the Credit Card List screen, the system populates all header fields with current application context information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the Credit Card List screen and card records have been read into the display array
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Screen data array population is performed for each of the 7 possible display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each row from 1 to 7: if the card data for that row is empty (equal to LOW-VALUES), the row is left blank and skipped; if the card data exists, the system populates the selection indicator field with the edit selection value (WS-EDIT-SELECT), the account number field with the account number (WS-ROW-ACCTNO), the card number field with the card number (WS-ROW-CARD-NUM), and the card status field with the card active status (WS-ROW-CARD-STATUS) for that row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Credit Card Data Row Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system populates up to 7 rows of credit card data on the list screen, skipping rows where no card data exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Screen row attribute setup is performed for each of the 7 possible display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For row 1: if the card data is empty (LOW-VALUES) OR the protect-select-rows flag is YES, set the selection field to protected-fset (DFHBMPRF); otherwise if the row has a selection error flag of '1', highlight the selection field in red (DFHRED) and if the selection value is space or low-values replace it with '*', then set the field to unprotected-fset (DFHBMFSE); for rows 2 through 7: if the card data is empty (LOW-VALUES) OR the protect-select-rows flag is YES, set the selection field to protected (DFHBMPRO); otherwise if the row has a selection error flag of '1', highlight the selection field in red (DFHRED) and set the cursor length to -1, then set the field to unprotected-fset (DFHBMFSE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Row Selection Field Attribute Setup
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system sets the display attributes for each of the 7 card row selection fields to control whether they are enterable, protected, or highlighted in red based on data and error state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Search filter display setup is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the session is a first-time entry (EIBCALEN=0) OR entering from the main menu program, the filter fields are left as-is; otherwise for the account ID filter: if the account filter is valid or in error, display the entered account ID value (CC-ACCT-ID) and set the field to unprotected-fset; if the CDEMO account ID is zero, clear the field to low-values; otherwise display the CDEMO account ID and set to unprotected-fset; for the card number filter: if the card filter is valid or in error, display the entered card number (CC-CARD-NUM) and set to unprotected-fset; if the CDEMO card number is zero, clear the field to low-values; otherwise display the CDEMO card number and set to unprotected-fset; additionally if the account filter is in error, highlight the account ID field in red and set cursor position to that field; if the card filter is in error, highlight the card number field in red and set cursor position to that field; if input is valid (INPUT-OK), set cursor position to the account ID field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Search Filter Field Display and Cursor Positioning
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system populates the account ID and card number filter fields on the screen and positions the cursor appropriately based on the current validation state of each filter.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Message setup is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system evaluates the current state in order: if the account filter is in error OR the card filter is in error, no message change is made (CONTINUE); else if PF7 was pressed AND the current page is the first page, set the error message to 'NO PREVIOUS PAGES TO DISPLAY'; else if PF8 was pressed AND no next page exists AND the last page was already shown, set the error message to 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY'; else if PF8 was pressed AND no next page exists (last page being shown for first time), set the informational message to the record action instructions message, and if the last page was not yet shown AND no next page exists, mark the last page as now shown; else if no informational message is set OR a next page exists, set the informational message to the record action instructions; else in all other cases, set the informational message to no-info-message; finally, move the error message to the screen error message field, and if an informational message is active AND it is not a no-records-found state, move the informational message text to the screen info message field and set the info message color to neutral

all_rules.Rule_Name: Informational and Error Message Setup for Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the screen, the system determines and sets the appropriate informational or error message based on the current navigation state and action context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Card List screen has been fully populated with header, data rows, filter fields, and messages
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen transmission step is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sends the screen map (LIT-THISMAP) from the mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET) using the populated output area (CCRDLIAO) to the terminal with cursor positioning enabled, erasing the previous screen content, and freeing the keyboard for user input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Transmission to Terminal
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system sends the fully populated Credit Card List screen to the user's terminal, replacing any previous screen content and releasing the keyboard for input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered data on the Credit Card List screen and pressed a key to submit
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the screen input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system receives the screen map (LIT-THISMAP) from the mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET) into the input area (CCRDLIAI), then extracts and stores: the account ID filter value (ACCTSIDI) into CC-ACCT-ID, the card number filter value (CARDSIDI) into CC-CARD-NUM, and the selection indicator values from all 7 rows (CRDSEL1I through CRDSEL7I) into WS-EDIT-SELECT positions 1 through 7 respectively

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Input Reception from Terminal
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system receives all user-entered data from the Credit Card List screen including filter values and row selection codes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Credit Card List screen with a value in the account ID filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Account filter validation is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system first sets the account filter flag to BLANK; if the account ID (CC-ACCT-ID) is equal to LOW-VALUES, SPACES, or zero (CC-ACCT-ID-N equals zeros), the system sets the account filter flag to BLANK, sets the CDEMO account ID to zero, and exits validation; if the account ID is not numeric, the system sets INPUT-ERROR to true, sets the account filter flag to NOT-OK, sets the protect-select-rows flag to YES, sets the error message to 'ACCOUNT FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 11 DIGIT NUMBER', sets the CDEMO account ID to zero, and exits validation; if the account ID is valid numeric, the system moves CC-ACCT-ID to CDEMO-ACCT-ID and sets the account filter flag to ISVALID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account ID Filter Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system validates the account ID filter entered by the user, determining whether it should be treated as no filter, an active filter, or an invalid entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Credit Card List screen with a value in the card number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Card number filter validation is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system first sets the card filter flag to BLANK; if the card number (CC-CARD-NUM) is equal to LOW-VALUES, SPACES, or zero (CC-CARD-NUM-N equals zeros), the system sets the card filter flag to BLANK, sets the CDEMO card number to zero, and exits validation; if the card number is not numeric, the system sets INPUT-ERROR to true, sets the card filter flag to NOT-OK, sets the protect-select-rows flag to YES, and if no prior error message exists (WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF is true) sets the error message to 'CARD ID FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 16 DIGIT NUMBER', sets the CDEMO card number to zero, and exits validation; if the card number is valid numeric, the system moves CC-CARD-NUM-N to CDEMO-CARD-NUM and sets the card filter flag to ISVALID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Filter Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system validates the card number filter entered by the user, determining whether it should be treated as no filter, an active filter, or an invalid entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Credit Card List screen with selection codes entered in one or more of the 7 card rows, and no prior input errors exist
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Row selection validation is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips validation if INPUT-ERROR is already true; otherwise it counts all occurrences of 'S' and 'U' across all 7 selection fields (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS); if the total count exceeds 1, the system sets INPUT-ERROR to true, sets the WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION flag to true, copies the selection flags to the error flags area, and replaces all 'S' and 'U' characters with '1' and all other characters with '0' in the error flags; then for each of the 7 rows the system evaluates: if the selection is valid (SELECT-OK - value is 'S' or 'U'), record the row index in I-SELECTED and if more-than-1-action is true mark that row's error flag as '1'; if the selection is blank (SELECT-BLANK), continue without action; if the selection is any other value, set INPUT-ERROR to true, mark that row's error flag as '1', and if no prior error message exists set the error message to indicate an invalid action code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Row Selection Code Validation - Single Selection Enforcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system validates that at most one row is selected and that all selection codes are valid, enforcing the business rule that only one card action can be performed per submission.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system needs to display a page of card records and a starting card key (WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM) has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Forward card record reading is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all 7 display rows to LOW-VALUES, opens a forward browse on the CARDDAT file starting at or after the given card key (GTEQ), initializes the screen row counter to zero, sets the next-page indicator to EXISTS and the read loop to MORE-RECORDS; for each record read: if the read is successful (NORMAL or DUPREC), the record is passed through the filter logic; if the record passes the filter, the row counter is incremented, the card number is stored in WS-ROW-CARD-NUM at the counter position, the account ID is stored in WS-ROW-ACCTNO at the counter position, the card active status is stored in WS-ROW-CARD-STATUS at the counter position; if this is the first qualifying record (counter=1), save the account ID to WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-ACCT-ID and the card number to WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM, and if the screen number is zero increment it by 1; if the row counter reaches the maximum screen lines (7), set the read loop to exit, save the current card account ID to WS-CA-LAST-CARD-ACCT-ID and card number to WS-CA-LAST-CARD-NUM, then perform a next-page existence check; if end-of-file is reached, set the read loop to exit, set next-page indicator to NOT-EXISTS, save the last card account ID and card number, and if no prior error message exists set the error message to 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW'; after the loop ends, close the browse on the CARDDAT file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Forward Card Record Browsing with Filter Application
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system browses the card file forward from a given starting key, reading up to 7 qualifying records per page while applying active account and card number filters, and tracking pagination bookmarks.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has been read from the CARDDAT file during a forward or backward browse operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record filter is applied
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system defaults to INCLUDE the record (WS-DONOT-EXCLUDE-THIS-RECORD is true); if the account filter is active (FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID is true), the system compares the record's account ID (CARD-ACCT-ID) to the filter account ID (CC-ACCT-ID): if they match, processing continues; if they do not match, the record is marked for EXCLUSION and filter processing ends; if the card number filter is active (FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID is true), the system compares the record's card number (CARD-NUM) to the filter card number (CC-CARD-NUM-N): if they match, processing continues; if they do not match, the record is marked for EXCLUSION and filter processing ends; records marked for exclusion are not added to the display rows

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Filter Application During File Browsing
all_rules.Rule_Description: During file browsing, each card record is evaluated against active account ID and card number filters to determine whether it should be included in or excluded from the display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully filled all 7 display rows with qualifying card records during a forward read
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The next page existence check is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs one additional READNEXT on the CARDDAT file; if the read is successful (NORMAL or DUPREC), the system sets the next-page indicator to EXISTS and updates WS-CA-LAST-CARD-ACCT-ID and WS-CA-LAST-CARD-NUM with this peeked record's values; if end-of-file is reached, the system sets the next-page indicator to NOT-EXISTS and if no prior error message exists sets the error message to 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW'; the read loop is then set to exit

all_rules.Rule_Name: Next Page Existence Check After Filling Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After filling the current page with 7 records, the system performs one additional read to determine whether more records exist, enabling correct display of the PF8 navigation option.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward read of card records has been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end of the card file is reached and the current screen number is 1 (first page) and the screen row counter is zero (no records were found)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the WS-NO-RECORDS-FOUND indicator to true, which suppresses normal informational messages and indicates to the user that no card records match the current filter criteria

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Records Found Notification on First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a forward read on the first page returns no qualifying records after applying filters, the system sets a no-records-found indicator to inform the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed processing a user interaction on the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session state persistence step is executed before returning to CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the transaction ID in the communication area to the current transaction ID, sets the originating program to the current program, sets the last mapset to the current mapset, sets the last map to the current map, copies the full CARDDEMO communication area into the work communication area, copies the program-specific communication area (containing first card key WS-CA-FIRST-CARDKEY, last card key WS-CA-LAST-CARDKEY, screen number WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM, and pagination state indicators) into the work communication area starting at the offset after the main communication area, then returns to CICS specifying the current transaction ID and the complete work communication area with its full length, causing CICS to re-invoke this transaction on the next user key press

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session State Persistence for Next Interaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each screen interaction, the system saves the complete session state to the communication area so it can be restored on the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program is started and there is no prior session context (communication area length is zero, indicating a fresh invocation with no carried-over state)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins its initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All working storage areas (CC-WORK-AREA), miscellaneous storage (WS-MISC-STORAGE), and the session communication area (WS-COMMAREA) must be fully cleared to their default empty values, and the error message display flag must be set to OFF so no stale error messages are carried forward

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Working Storage and Session Variables on Fresh Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card List program is invoked for the first time with no prior session context, all working storage areas, miscellaneous storage, and the session communication area must be cleared to ensure no residual data from previous sessions affects the current execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program is starting a fresh session with no prior context (communication area length is zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes session identity fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) must be stored in the working storage transaction ID field (WS-TRANID) AND also recorded in the application communication area's originating transaction ID field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), so both the local session and the shared communication area reflect the correct transaction identity

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Transaction ID at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program startup, the system must record the current transaction identifier in both the general working storage transaction field and the application communication area's originating transaction field, establishing the identity of the transaction for the current session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program is invoked and the communication area length is zero, confirming this is a brand-new session with no data passed from a prior program execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program performs its fresh-start initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The application-wide communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be fully initialized to default empty values, AND the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must also be fully initialized to default empty values, ensuring no residual data from any prior session exists in either area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Application and Program Communication Areas on Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card List program is entered for the first time with no prior session data, both the shared application-level communication area and the program-specific communication area must be fully initialized to blank/default values to prevent any unintended data inheritance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program is starting a fresh session (communication area length is zero) and the application communication area has been initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets its identity in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program's name (LIT-THISPGM) must be stored in the communication area's originating program field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), so any downstream program or screen can identify the Card List program as the source of the current transaction flow

all_rules.Rule_Name: Register Program Name as the Originating Program in Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: During fresh program initialization, the system must record the current program's own name as the originating program in the application communication area. This establishes the program's identity so that subsequent screens and programs can identify where control originated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program is starting a fresh session (communication area length is zero) and the communication area has been initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets the user role for the session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The user type indicator in the application communication area (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER) must be set to TRUE, designating the current session as a Standard User session, which governs the level of access and actions available to the user on the card list screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Standard User Type to the Current Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card List program initializes a fresh session, the user type must be set to Standard User in the communication area. This establishes the access level and role context for the session, ensuring the user is treated as a regular (non-administrative) user throughout the card list interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program is starting a fresh session (communication area length is zero) and the communication area has been initialized with the program name and user type
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets its entry status
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program entry status flag in the application communication area (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) must be set to TRUE, indicating this is a fresh program entry. This flag distinguishes a first-time entry from a re-entry after returning from a detail or update screen, and controls how the program processes subsequent user interactions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Program Status as Fresh Entry in Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: During fresh program initialization, the program status must be flagged as a new entry (first-time entry) in the communication area. This status flag signals to the program's own logic and any called programs that the user is entering this screen for the first time, not returning from a sub-screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program is starting a fresh session (communication area length is zero) and the communication area has been initialized with program identity and entry status
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program registers the current screen references
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current screen map name (LIT-THISMAP) must be stored in the communication area's last-used map field (CDEMO-LAST-MAP), AND the current map set name (LIT-THISMAPSET) must be stored in the communication area's last-used map set field (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), so the system can correctly identify and return to the Card List screen when navigating back from other screens

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Screen Map and Map Set References in Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: During fresh program initialization, the system must record the current screen map name and map set name in the application communication area. These references identify which screen layout is currently active and are used for screen navigation and return routing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program is starting a fresh session (communication area length is zero) and the communication area has been initialized with program identity, user type, entry status, and screen map references
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets the initial pagination state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first-page indicator (CA-FIRST-PAGE) must be set to TRUE, signaling that the current display position is at the beginning of the card record list. This flag prevents backward navigation (PF7) from being processed and ensures the forward read begins from the first available card record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Pagination to First Page on Fresh Program Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card List program starts a fresh session, the pagination state must be set to indicate the user is on the first page of card records. This ensures that the initial display begins from the very first available card record and that backward navigation (PF7) is correctly disabled.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program is starting a fresh session (communication area length is zero) and the pagination has been set to the first page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets the last-page display tracking state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The last-page-shown indicator (CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN) must be set to TRUE, recording that the last page of card records has not yet been displayed to the user. This distinction is critical: when the user first reaches the last page, an informational message about available actions is shown; only on a subsequent PF8 press at the last page is the 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY' message shown

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Last Page as Not Yet Displayed on Fresh Program Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card List program starts a fresh session, the last-page-shown indicator must be set to 'not yet shown'. This ensures that when the user eventually reaches the last page of card records, the system correctly identifies it as being seen for the first time and displays the appropriate informational message rather than a 'no more pages' message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is returning to the Card List program and a prior session context exists (communication area length is greater than zero), indicating this is not a first-time entry into the program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects an active communication area from the previous session interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system restores the general application-wide session data from the first segment of the communication area into the application context, making available: the originating transaction identifier (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), the originating program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), the user type indicator (CDEMO-USRTYP), the last map name (CDEMO-LAST-MAP), the last mapset name (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), the account ID filter (CDEMO-ACCT-ID), and the card number filter (CDEMO-CARD-NUM)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restore General Application Session Context on Program Re-entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user returns to the Card List program (not a first-time entry), the system must restore the previously saved application-wide session data from the first portion of the communication area. This includes the originating transaction identifier, originating program name, user type, last map name, last mapset name, account ID, and card number that were active in the prior session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is returning to the Card List program and a prior session context exists (communication area length is greater than zero), and the general application context has already been restored from the first segment of the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the second portion of the communication area, starting immediately after the general application context segment, for a length equal to the program-specific communication area size
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system restores the program-specific card list session data into the program working storage, making available: the first card number bookmark of the current page (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM) used for backward navigation, the last card number bookmark of the current page (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-NUM) used for forward navigation, the current page/screen number (WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM), the first-page position flag (CA-FIRST-PAGE), the next-page existence flag (CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS or CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS), and the last-page-shown flag (CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN or CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restore Program-Specific Pagination and Navigation State on Re-entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user returns to the Card List program, the system must restore the program-specific session data from the second portion of the communication area. This includes the card list pagination state such as the first card key on the current page, the last card key on the current page, the current screen/page number, and the pagination position flags (first page indicator, next page existence indicator, last page shown indicator).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is returning to the Card List program with a valid prior session (communication area length greater than zero), and both the general application context and the program-specific context restoration steps have been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Both communication area segments have been successfully read and mapped to their respective working storage areas
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete session state is available for use, including: the first card number key (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM) identifying the starting record of the currently displayed page, the last card number key (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-NUM) identifying the ending record of the currently displayed page, the current screen/page number (WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM) for display in the page number field, and the pagination state flags indicating whether the user is on the first page, whether a next page of records exists, and whether the last page has already been shown to the user — enabling the program to correctly handle PF7 (previous page), PF8 (next page) navigation and display appropriate messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session Context Availability After Restoration
all_rules.Rule_Description: After both the general application context and the program-specific context have been restored from the communication area, the complete session state is available for the program to use in subsequent processing. The card list can resume exactly where the user left off, with all pagination bookmarks and navigation state intact.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Card List program is invoked and a prior session communication area exists
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program entry mode indicator (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) is set to TRUE indicating a fresh entry AND the originating program identifier (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) is NOT equal to the current Card List program identifier (LIT-THISPGM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system recognizes this as a fresh entry from a different program and proceeds to reset all session context, pagination state, and screen indicators before displaying the card list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Fresh Entry from a Different Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the user is entering the Credit Card List screen fresh from another program (such as the main menu), as opposed to returning to the same screen from a prior interaction. Both conditions must be true simultaneously: the program must be in 'enter' mode AND the originating program must be different from the current Card List program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected that the user is entering the Credit Card List screen fresh from a different program (entry mode is fresh AND originating program differs from current program)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fresh entry condition is confirmed as TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) is cleared and re-initialized to its default empty state, removing all prior pagination bookmarks, card key values, screen counters, filter flags, and row selection data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset All Session Context on Fresh Program Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters the Credit Card List screen fresh from another program, all previously stored session-specific data for this program must be cleared. This includes pagination bookmarks (first and last card numbers), screen counters, filter states, and any row selection data carried over from a prior session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed a fresh entry from a different program and has cleared all prior session context data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session context reset is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program entry mode indicator (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) is set to TRUE, marking the current interaction as a fresh program entry so that downstream processing treats this as a new session start

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Program State as Fresh Entry Mode
all_rules.Rule_Description: After resetting session context on a fresh entry from another program, the program entry mode indicator must be explicitly re-affirmed as 'entering' to ensure subsequent processing logic correctly identifies this as a new session start rather than a re-entry or return.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed a fresh entry from a different program and has set the program entry mode to fresh start
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program entry mode indicator is re-affirmed as fresh entry
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The last active screen identifier (CDEMO-LAST-MAP) is set to the current Card List screen map name (LIT-THISMAP), establishing the Card List screen as the current active screen in the session navigation context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Screen as Last Active Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When starting a fresh session on the Credit Card List screen, the system must record the current screen identifier as the last active screen in the session context. This ensures that navigation history and return-path tracking are correctly initialized to the Card List screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed a fresh entry from a different program and has recorded the current screen as the last active screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen context is established for the new session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The pagination position indicator (CA-FIRST-PAGE) is set to TRUE, signaling that the card list display should begin from the very first page of available card records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Pagination to Beginning of Card List
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters the Credit Card List screen fresh from another program, the pagination position must be reset to the very beginning of the card list so that the user always starts viewing cards from the first available record, regardless of any prior navigation position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed a fresh entry from a different program and has reset the pagination position to the first page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first-page pagination indicator is set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The last-page display tracking indicator (CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN) is set to TRUE, marking that the last page of card records has NOT yet been displayed in this session, so that end-of-list messages and next-page availability checks are correctly evaluated during subsequent navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Last Page Display Indicator for New Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When starting a fresh session on the Credit Card List screen, the indicator tracking whether the last page of card records has been displayed must be reset. This ensures that end-of-list messaging and navigation behavior are correctly re-initialized, preventing stale 'last page already shown' state from a prior session from affecting the new session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed any function key or action key on the Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the function key validation process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must first mark the pressed key status as INVALID before performing any further key recognition checks, ensuring no key is assumed valid without explicit verification

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default All Function Keys to Invalid Status Before Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any key validation occurs, the system marks the currently pressed function key as invalid by default. This ensures that only explicitly recognized keys are treated as valid actions, preventing unintended behavior from unrecognized key presses.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has defaulted the pressed key status to INVALID and is evaluating the key pressed by the user on the Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the pressed key is one of the four allowed keys: Enter (submit/select action), PF3 (exit to main menu), PF7 (navigate to previous page), or PF8 (navigate to next page)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the pressed key matches Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8, the system marks the key status as VALID and proceeds with the corresponding key action; if the pressed key does not match any of these four allowed keys, the key status remains INVALID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Pressed Key Against Allowed Function Keys
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card List screen only recognizes four specific keys as valid actions: Enter, PF3, PF7, and PF8. The system checks whether the pressed key matches any of these four allowed keys and marks it as valid if a match is found. Any key not in this set remains marked as invalid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Card List screen that is not Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8, and the key status has been marked as INVALID after the allowed-key check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects that the key status is still INVALID after the allowed-key validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system overrides the pressed key and sets the active key action to ENTER, so that all subsequent processing treats the interaction as an Enter key press with its default submit behavior, without displaying any error message to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Override Unrecognized Key Press to Default Enter Key Behavior
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses a key that is not one of the four recognized keys (Enter, PF3, PF7, PF8), the system does not reject the interaction or display an error. Instead, it silently overrides the unrecognized key and treats the action as if the user had pressed the Enter key, applying the default Enter key behavior.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Card List screen and presses PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the originating program recorded in the communication area matches the Card List program identifier (LIT-THISPGM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the originating program matches the Card List program, the system proceeds with the exit-to-menu workflow; if the originating program does NOT match (user arrived from a different program), the system bypasses the immediate exit and continues with normal program processing including a forward read and screen redisplay

all_rules.Rule_Name: Verify User Origin Before Allowing PF3 Exit to Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before processing a PF3 exit request, the system must verify that the user is currently operating within the Card List program itself (not arriving from a different program). Only users who are actively within this program are permitted to exit directly to the main menu via PF3.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3 and the system has confirmed the user is currently within the Card List program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the communication area for transfer to the main menu
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction identifier (LIT-THISTRANID) is recorded as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), and the current program name (LIT-THISPGM) is recorded as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program Context in Communication Area on PF3 Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid PF3 exit is confirmed, the system must update the shared communication area to record the current Card List transaction and program as the source of the navigation, ensuring the main menu knows where the user came from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed a valid PF3 exit and has updated the communication area with the current program context
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the session state flags in the communication area prior to transferring control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The user type flag is set to standard user (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER = TRUE) and the program entry mode is set to fresh entry (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE), indicating the destination program should initialize as if the user is entering for the first time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set User Entry Mode to Fresh Entry on PF3 Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When transferring control to the main menu via PF3, the system must mark the session state so that the main menu program treats the incoming navigation as a fresh program entry by a standard user, not a re-entry from a prior interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has set the user entry mode to fresh entry and is preparing to transfer control to the main menu
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the navigation destination fields in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET) is recorded as the last mapset (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), the current map (LIT-THISMAP) is recorded as the last map (CDEMO-LAST-MAP), the main menu program name (LIT-MENUPGM) is set as the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM), the main menu mapset (LIT-MENUMAPSET) is set as the next mapset (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET), and the current map (LIT-THISMAP) is set as the next map (CCARD-NEXT-MAP)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Navigation Targets to Main Menu Program on PF3 Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When exiting to the main menu via PF3, the system must record the current screen context and designate the main menu program and its associated map/mapset as the intended navigation destination in the communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has fully prepared the communication area with source context, user entry mode, and navigation targets for the PF3 exit
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the final preparation step before invoking the transfer to the main menu
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The exit message indicator (WS-EXIT-MESSAGE) is set to TRUE, signaling that the user has chosen to exit the Card List program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Exit Message Indicator Before Transferring to Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: Immediately before transferring control to the main menu, the system must activate the exit message indicator flag to signal that the user has intentionally exited the Card List screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The exit message indicator has been set and all communication area fields have been populated with the current program context, user entry mode, and navigation targets
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer instruction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred directly to the main menu program (LIT-MENUPGM / COMEN01C) via an XCTL call, passing the complete CARDDEMO-COMMAREA communication area; the Card List program terminates its current execution and the main menu program is displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Main Menu Program on PF3 Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all communication area fields have been updated and the exit indicator has been set, the system must immediately transfer control to the main menu program (COMEN01C), passing the fully updated communication area so the main menu has complete context about the user's session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user presses PF3 but the originating program recorded in the communication area does NOT match the Card List program identifier (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM NOT EQUAL LIT-THISPGM), or the program is in re-entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) from a different program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the PF3 action in the main routing logic
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets both the shared communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), sets the originating transaction to the current transaction (LIT-THISTRANID in CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), sets the originating program to the current program (LIT-THISPGM in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), sets user type to standard user (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER = TRUE), sets program mode to fresh entry (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE), records the current map and mapset (LIT-THISMAP in CDEMO-LAST-MAP, LIT-THISMAPSET in CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), resets the page position to the first page (CA-FIRST-PAGE = TRUE, CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN = TRUE), performs a forward read of card records starting from the first card number bookmark (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM), and redisplays the Card List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Normal Processing When PF3 Pressed from a Different Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF3 is pressed but the user did not arrive from the Card List program itself (i.e., the session originated from a different program), the system must not exit to the main menu. Instead, it must reset the session state, perform a fresh forward read of card records, and redisplay the Card List screen as if entering for the first time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen and a session is active with an existing last page display status (either 'Last Page Shown' or 'Last Page Not Yet Shown')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 (Page Down key) to navigate to the next page of card records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must keep the current 'last page displayed' indicator completely unchanged — if it was previously marked as 'Last Page Shown', it remains 'Last Page Shown'; if it was marked as 'Last Page Not Yet Shown', it remains 'Last Page Not Yet Shown' — so that subsequent page navigation and end-of-list messaging logic can operate on the accurate, unaltered pagination state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Last Page Display Status on PF8 Page Down
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 (Page Down) to navigate forward through the card list, the system must preserve the existing 'last page displayed' indicator without modification, ensuring that the pagination state accurately reflects whether the last page has already been shown to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen and the 'last page displayed' indicator may currently be set to either 'Last Page Shown' or 'Last Page Not Yet Shown'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than PF8 — specifically ENTER (to submit filters or select a card action), PF3 (to exit to the main menu), PF7 (to navigate to the previous page), or any unrecognized/invalid key that is defaulted to ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must reset the 'last page displayed' indicator to 'Last Page Not Yet Shown', clearing any prior record of the last page having been displayed, so that forward pagination logic and end-of-list messaging (such as 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY') will be accurately re-evaluated on the next PF8 navigation attempt

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Last Page Display Indicator on Non-PF8 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user performs any action other than pressing PF8 (Page Down) — including pressing ENTER, PF3 (Exit), PF7 (Page Up), or any invalid key — the system must reset the 'last page displayed' indicator to 'Not Yet Displayed'. This ensures that if the user navigates away from the last page and returns, the system correctly re-evaluates and re-presents the end-of-list condition rather than incorrectly suppressing the 'no more pages' message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card List screen and has entered a value in the Account ID filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Account ID filter value is not blank, not zero, and is NOT a numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the input state to ERROR, (2) Mark the Account Filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK), (3) Set the error message to 'ACCOUNT FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 11 DIGIT NUMBER', (4) Set the Account ID in the session to zero, (5) Protect all 7 card selection rows from user input so no row action can be selected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Filter Non-Numeric Validation Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a non-numeric value in the Account ID filter field, the system must reject the input, set a specific error message, and prevent any row selections from being made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID filter field is blank, contains only spaces, contains only low-values, or its numeric equivalent equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Mark the Account Filter as blank (FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK), (2) Set the session Account ID to zero, (3) Apply no account-based filtering to the card list, (4) Continue processing without setting any error condition

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Filter Blank or Zero Treated as No Filter
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID filter field is left blank or contains zero, the system treats it as no filter being applied and allows processing to continue without error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card List screen and has entered a value in the Card Number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Card Number filter value is not blank, not zero, and is NOT a numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the input state to ERROR, (2) Mark the Card Filter as invalid (FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK), (3) Set the error message to 'CARD ID FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 16 DIGIT NUMBER' only if no prior error message has already been set, (4) Set the session Card Number to zero, (5) Protect all 7 card selection rows from user input so no row action can be selected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Filter Non-Numeric Validation Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a non-numeric value in the Card Number filter field, the system must reject the input, set a specific error message, and prevent any row selections from being made.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card Number filter field is blank, contains only spaces, contains only low-values, or its numeric equivalent equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Mark the Card Filter as blank (FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK), (2) Set the session Card Number to zero, (3) Apply no card-number-based filtering to the card list, (4) Continue processing without setting any error condition

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Filter Blank or Zero Treated as No Filter
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card Number filter field is left blank or contains zero, the system treats it as no filter being applied and allows processing to continue without error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card List screen and has entered action codes (S for View or U for Update) in the selection fields of the displayed card rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The total count of rows containing 'S' (View) or 'U' (Update) across all 7 selection fields is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the input state to ERROR, (2) Set the WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION flag to TRUE, (3) Copy the selection flags to an error flags array, (4) In the error flags array, replace every 'S' and every 'U' with '1' and all other characters with '0' to mark exactly which rows had selections, (5) Keep all 7 card selection rows accessible (not protected) so the user can correct the selection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Multiple Row Selections Not Allowed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters action codes in more than one row simultaneously, the system must reject the submission, mark all rows that had selections as errors, and display an appropriate error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card List screen and has entered a value in one or more of the 7 row selection fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A row selection field contains a value that is not 'S' (View), not 'U' (Update), and not blank or space
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the input state to ERROR, (2) Set the error indicator '1' for that specific row in the row error flags array, (3) Set the error message to indicate an invalid action code only if no prior error message has already been set (WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF is true), (4) Keep all 7 card selection rows accessible (not protected) so the user can correct the entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Action Code in Row Selection Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a value other than 'S', 'U', or blank in a row selection field, the system must mark that specific row as having an error and set an invalid action code error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Credit Card List screen with filter values entered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either the Account ID filter is marked as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK) OR the Card Number filter is marked as invalid (FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set all 7 row selection fields (CRDSEL1 through CRDSEL7) to protected/non-enterable attribute (DFHBMPRF for row 1, DFHBMPRO for rows 2-7) so the user cannot enter any action code until the filter errors are corrected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Protect All Selection Rows When Filter Validation Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: When either the Account ID filter or the Card Number filter fails validation, all 7 row selection fields on the screen must be protected (made non-enterable) to prevent the user from attempting row actions while filter errors exist.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected an input error condition on the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The input error exists AND the Account ID filter is NOT marked as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is false) AND the Card Number filter is NOT marked as invalid (FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK is false)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must perform a forward read of credit card records (9000-READ-FORWARD) starting from the current card position bookmark, applying any active account or card number filters, to populate up to 7 card rows for display alongside the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditional Forward Record Read When Input Error Exists but Filters Are Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an input error exists (such as an invalid row selection) but both the Account ID filter and Card Number filter are individually valid, the system still performs a forward read of card records to populate the list for display context before showing the error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has detected an input error condition on the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID filter is marked as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is true) OR the Card Number filter is marked as invalid (FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must skip the forward read of card records entirely and proceed directly to setting up the error message display and re-rendering the screen without attempting to read any card data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Record Read When Filter Errors Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an input error exists and at least one filter field (Account ID or Card Number) is invalid, the system skips the forward record read entirely and proceeds directly to re-displaying the screen with error indicators.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An input error has been detected and the system is preparing to re-display the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The input error flag is set to TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Move the error message text (WS-ERROR-MSG) to the screen error message output field (ERRMSGO), (2) Set the current program as both the source program and the next program to navigate to, (3) Set the current map and mapset as both the last used and the next to display, ensuring the user remains on the Card List screen after the error is shown

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Message Propagation to Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an input error condition exists, the system must transfer the error message text to the screen output area and set up the next program navigation context to remain on the Card List screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to re-display the Credit Card List screen after an input error
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID filter is marked as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the Account ID filter field color attribute to RED (DFHRED), (2) Set the cursor length indicator for the Account ID field to -1 to position the cursor at that field on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Invalid Account Filter Field in Red
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID filter field contains an invalid value, the system must visually highlight it in red on the screen and position the cursor to it so the user can immediately identify and correct the error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to re-display the Credit Card List screen after an input error
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card Number filter is marked as invalid (FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the Card Number filter field color attribute to RED (DFHRED), (2) Set the cursor length indicator for the Card Number field to -1 to position the cursor at that field on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Invalid Card Number Filter Field in Red
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card Number filter field contains an invalid value, the system must visually highlight it in red on the screen and position the cursor to it so the user can immediately identify and correct the error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to re-display the Credit Card List screen after a row selection validation error
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A row's error indicator flag (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR) is set to '1' for any of the 7 card rows
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must for each affected row: (1) Set that row's selection field color attribute to RED (DFHRED), (2) Set the cursor length indicator for that row's selection field to -1 to position the cursor there. Additionally, for row 1 specifically: if the selection field is blank or low-values, display an asterisk '*' in the field to visually indicate the error position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Invalid Row Selection Fields in Red
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a row selection field contains an invalid action code or is part of a multiple-selection error, the system must visually highlight that specific row's selection field in red and position the cursor to it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The overall input state is valid (INPUT-OK is true), meaning no account filter errors and no card filter errors are present
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the cursor length indicator for the Account ID filter field (ACCTSIDL) to -1 to position the cursor at the Account ID field, ready for the user's next input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioning to First Error Field When Input is Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no filter validation errors exist and the input is considered valid, the system positions the cursor at the Account ID filter field as the default starting position for the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed setting up error messages, field highlights, and cursor positioning for the Credit Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An input error condition exists and the screen preparation steps (screen init, array population, attribute setup, message setup) have all been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Send the fully prepared Credit Card List screen (map CCRDLIAO within mapset LIT-THISMAPSET) to the user's terminal with ERASE to clear the previous screen and FREEKB to release the keyboard, (2) Save the current session state including program name, transaction ID, map name, and mapset name to the communication area, (3) Return control to CICS specifying the same transaction ID so the system awaits the user's next corrective input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-display Card List Screen with Error Indicators
all_rules.Rule_Description: After setting up all error messages and field highlights, the system sends the complete Credit Card List screen back to the user with all error indicators visible, then returns control awaiting the user's corrective input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is validating inputs on the Credit Card List screen and an error message has already been set by a prior validation check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A subsequent validation check (such as card filter error or invalid row action code) also detects an error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must NOT overwrite the existing error message. The new error message is only set if the error message flag (WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF) indicates that no prior error message has been set. This ensures the first detected error message is the one displayed to the user.

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Error Message Priority Rule
all_rules.Rule_Description: When multiple validation errors could potentially set error messages, only the first error message encountered is retained. Subsequent error conditions do not overwrite an already-set error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen and the current page is flagged as the First Page (CA-FIRST-PAGE is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 (Page Up)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system recognises that no previous page exists and proceeds to re-read and redisplay the same first page of card records, rather than attempting to navigate backward

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Page Up Request on First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF7 (Page Up) and the current page is already the first page of card results, the system identifies this condition and routes to the first-page re-display logic instead of attempting backward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 while already on the first page of card results, and the session state holds a saved First Card Number (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM) representing the first card displayed on the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to re-read the first page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the card file read position to the saved First Card Number (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM), so that the forward read begins from the same starting card as the currently displayed first page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve First Card Key for Re-display
