Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card list screen is being prepared for display and Row 2 of the card data array is empty (contains no card record data)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether Row 2 has data available to display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Row 2 is skipped entirely with no data populated on the screen for that row, and the system proceeds to evaluate Row 3

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Empty Card Row 2 During Screen Population

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card list screen is being prepared for display and Row 2 of the card data array contains a valid credit card record (data is not empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that Row 2 has data available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates all four fields for Row 2 on the screen: (1) the Selection Indicator field is set from the row's edit-select value, (2) the Account Number field is set from the row's account number value, (3) the Card Number field is set from the row's card number value, and (4) the Card Active Status field is set from the row's card status value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Card Data for Row 2
all_rules.Rule_Description: When Row 2 of the card data array contains a valid credit card record, all four data fields for that row are populated on the screen: the selection indicator, the account number, the card number, and the card active status.

Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Row 3 is skipped entirely with no data populated on the screen for that row, and the system proceeds to evaluate Row 4

all_rules.Rule_Description: When Row 3 of the card data array contains a valid credit card record, all four data fields for that row are populated on the screen: the selection indicator, the account number, the card number, and the card active status.

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether Row 5 has data available to display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Row 5 is skipped entirely with no data populated on the screen for that row, and the system proceeds to evaluate Row 6

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Empty Card Row 5 During Screen Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: When populating the card list screen, Row 5 is only filled with card data if it contains a valid record. If Row 5 has no data, it is silently skipped and the system moves on to evaluate Row 6.

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that Row 5 has data available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates all four fields for Row 5 on the screen: (1) the Selection Indicator field is set from the row's edit-select value, (2) the Account Number field is set from the row's account number value, (3) the Card Number field is set from the row's card number value, and (4) the Card Active Status field is set from the row's card status value

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether Row 6 has data available to display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Row 6 is skipped entirely with no data populated on the screen for that row, and the system proceeds to evaluate Row 7

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Empty Card Row 6 During Screen Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: When populating the card list screen, Row 6 is only filled with card data if it contains a valid record. If Row 6 has no data, it is silently skipped and the system moves on to evaluate Row 7.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card list screen is being prepared for display and Row 6 of the card data array contains a valid credit card record (data is not empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that Row 6 has data available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates all four fields for Row 6 on the screen: (1) the Selection Indicator field is set from the row's edit-select value, (2) the Account Number field is set from the row's account number value, (3) the Card Number field is set from the row's card number value, and (4) the Card Active Status field is set from the row's card status value

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether Row 7 has data available to display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Row 7 is skipped entirely with no data populated on the screen for that row, and the screen array population process completes with all available rows having been evaluated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Empty Card Row 7 During Screen Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: When populating the card list screen, Row 7 is only filled with card data if it contains a valid record. If Row 7 has no data, it is silently skipped and the screen array population is complete.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card list screen is being prepared for display and Row 7 of the card data array contains a valid credit card record (data is not empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that Row 7 has data available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates all four fields for Row 7 on the screen: (1) the Selection Indicator field is set from the row's edit-select value, (2) the Account Number field is set from the row's account number value, (3) the Card Number field is set from the row's card number value, and (4) the Card Active Status field is set from the row's card status value, and the screen array population process completes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Card Data for Row 7
all_rules.Rule_Description: When Row 7 of the card data array contains a valid credit card record, all four data fields for that row are populated on the screen: the selection indicator, the account number, the card number, and the card active status. This is the final row and completes the screen array population.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card list screen is being prepared for display and a card selection row (any of rows 1 through 7) contains no card data (row data equals LOW-VALUES)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the display attributes for that row's selection field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The selection field for that row is set to protected mode, preventing the user from entering any value in that field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Protect Card Selection Field for Empty Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card list display row contains no card data, the selection field for that row must be protected so the user cannot enter a selection action on an empty row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card list screen is being prepared for display and the system has flagged that selection rows must be protected due to input validation errors (e.g., invalid account filter or invalid card filter)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the display attributes for each of the 7 card selection rows
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 7 card selection fields are set to protected mode regardless of whether the rows contain card data, preventing the user from entering any selection value on any row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Protect All Card Selection Fields When Input Errors Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account or card filter validation errors exist, all card selection fields across all 7 rows must be protected to prevent the user from attempting to select a card while filter inputs are invalid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card list screen is being prepared for display, a card selection row (any of rows 1 through 7) contains card data, the rows are not globally protected, and the row's selection error indicator is set to '1'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the display attributes for that row's selection field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The selection field for that row is highlighted in red color to indicate an error condition on that specific row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Card Selection Field in Red When Row Has a Selection Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card row contains data and is not protected, but the user entered an invalid or conflicting selection value on that row, the selection field must be visually highlighted in red to draw attention to the error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card list screen is being prepared for display, row 1 contains card data, the row is not globally protected, row 1 has a selection error indicator set to '1', and the current selection value for row 1 is a space or LOW-VALUES (blank or empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the display attributes for row 1's selection field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The selection field for row 1 is populated with the asterisk character '*' as an error symbol to indicate a missing required selection value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark First Row Selection Field with Error Symbol When Value is Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: For the first card row specifically, when a selection error exists but the selection field is blank or empty, the system must place an asterisk '*' symbol in the field to visually indicate that an action was expected but not provided.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card list screen is being prepared for display, a card selection row (any of rows 1 through 7) contains card data, the rows are not globally protected due to input errors, and the row has no selection error indicator set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the display attributes for that row's selection field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The selection field for that row is set to an enterable and storable mode, allowing the user to type a selection action code ('S' for View or 'U' for Update) into that field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Make Card Selection Field Enterable When Row Has Valid Data and No Errors
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card row contains valid card data, the rows are not globally protected, and there is no selection error on that row, the selection field must be made enterable so the user can input a valid action code (View 'S' or Update 'U').

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card list screen is being prepared for display with up to 7 card records loaded into the display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the screen row attribute setup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each of the 7 card selection rows (rows 1 through 7) is individually evaluated and configured with the correct display attribute — protected if empty or globally protected, red-highlighted if a selection error exists, or enterable if the row has valid data and no errors — and all 7 rows are processed before the screen is sent to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Process All 7 Card Selection Rows for Attribute Configuration
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen attribute setup must evaluate and configure every one of the 7 card selection rows individually, applying the appropriate display state (protected, error-highlighted, or enterable) to each row based on its specific data and error conditions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is accessing the Card List screen either for the first time (fresh program entry with no prior session) or has navigated from the Main Menu program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display setup is being prepared to render the search filter fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account ID filter field and card number filter field are left at their default values without being populated from session data or prior filter values; no filter values are pre-filled on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Filter Field Population on Fresh Entry or Menu Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card List screen is accessed for the first time or navigated to from the Main Menu, the account ID and card number search filter fields are left at their default values and not populated from session data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is returning to the Card List screen after a prior interaction, and the account ID filter field has been validated and marked as valid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display setup is preparing the account ID filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current account ID value (CC-ACCT-ID) is displayed in the account ID filter field on the screen, and the field attribute is set to allow user entry (field is unprotected and editable)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Valid Account ID Filter Value on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account ID filter has been validated as a valid numeric value, the current account ID filter value is displayed in the account ID filter field on the screen and the field is made available for user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is returning to the Card List screen after a prior interaction, and the account ID filter field has been marked as having a validation error (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display setup is preparing the account ID filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The erroneous account ID value (CC-ACCT-ID) that was entered by the user is displayed in the account ID filter field on the screen, and the field attribute is set to allow user entry so the user can correct the invalid value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Account ID Error Value in Filter Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account ID filter has a validation error, the erroneous value entered by the user is retained and displayed in the account ID filter field so the user can correct it, and the field remains editable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is returning to the Card List screen, the account ID filter is in a blank/neutral state (neither FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID nor FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK), and the account ID stored in the session (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display setup is preparing the account ID filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account ID filter field on the screen is cleared (set to low-values/empty), displaying no value to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Account ID Filter Field When Session Account ID Is Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account ID filter is neither valid nor in error (blank state), and the session account ID value is zero, the account ID filter field is cleared on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is returning to the Card List screen, the account ID filter is in a blank/neutral state (neither FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID nor FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK), and the account ID stored in the session (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) is a non-zero value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display setup is preparing the account ID filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session account ID value (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) is displayed in the account ID filter field on the screen, and the field attribute is set to allow user entry (field is unprotected and editable)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Session Account ID Value When Non-Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account ID filter is in a neutral state and the session contains a non-zero account ID value, that session account ID is displayed in the filter field and made editable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is returning to the Card List screen after a prior interaction, and the card number filter field has been validated and marked as valid (FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display setup is preparing the card number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current card number value (CC-CARD-NUM) is displayed in the card number filter field on the screen, and the field attribute is set to allow user entry (field is unprotected and editable)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Valid Card Number Filter Value on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number filter has been validated as a valid numeric value, the current card number filter value is displayed in the card number filter field on the screen and the field is made available for user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is returning to the Card List screen after a prior interaction, and the card number filter field has been marked as having a validation error (FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display setup is preparing the card number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The erroneous card number value (CC-CARD-NUM) that was entered by the user is displayed in the card number filter field on the screen, and the field attribute is set to allow user entry so the user can correct the invalid value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Card Number Error Value in Filter Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number filter has a validation error, the erroneous value entered by the user is retained and displayed in the card number filter field so the user can correct it, and the field remains editable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is returning to the Card List screen, the card number filter is in a blank/neutral state (neither FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID nor FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK), and the card number stored in the session (CDEMO-CARD-NUM) equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display setup is preparing the card number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card number filter field on the screen is cleared (set to low-values/empty), displaying no value to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Card Number Filter Field When Session Card Number Is Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number filter is neither valid nor in error (blank state), and the session card number value is zero, the card number filter field is cleared on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is returning to the Card List screen, the card number filter is in a blank/neutral state (neither FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID nor FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK), and the card number stored in the session (CDEMO-CARD-NUM) is a non-zero value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen display setup is preparing the card number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session card number value (CDEMO-CARD-NUM) is displayed in the card number filter field on the screen, and the field attribute is set to allow user entry (field is unprotected and editable)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Session Card Number Value When Non-Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number filter is in a neutral state and the session contains a non-zero card number value, that session card number is displayed in the filter field and made editable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List screen is being prepared for display and the account ID filter field has been marked as having a validation error (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen field attributes are being set up for the account ID filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account ID filter field color attribute is set to red (DFHRED) to visually indicate the error, and the cursor length attribute is set to position the cursor at the account ID filter field (ACCTSIDL set to -1), directing the user to correct the invalid account ID value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Account ID Filter Field in Red When Validation Error Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account ID filter field contains an invalid value, the field is visually highlighted in red on the screen and the cursor is automatically positioned at the account ID field to direct the user to correct the error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List screen is being prepared for display and the card number filter field has been marked as having a validation error (FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen field attributes are being set up for the card number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card number filter field color attribute is set to red (DFHRED) to visually indicate the error, and the cursor length attribute is set to position the cursor at the card number filter field (CARDSIDL set to -1), directing the user to correct the invalid card number value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Card Number Filter Field in Red When Validation Error Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number filter field contains an invalid value, the field is visually highlighted in red on the screen and the cursor is automatically positioned at the card number field to direct the user to correct the error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List screen is being prepared for display and all input validations have passed with no errors (INPUT-OK is true, meaning neither account filter nor card filter has a validation error)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen field attributes are being finalized after all validation checks
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor length attribute for the account ID filter field (ACCTSIDL) is set to -1, which positions the cursor at the account ID filter field as the default entry point for the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Position Cursor at Account ID Field When All Inputs Are Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all input fields on the Card List screen are valid with no errors, the cursor is automatically positioned at the account ID filter field as the default starting point for user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Card List screen and has submitted the screen with filter values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either the Account ID filter or the Card Number filter has a validation error (invalid non-numeric value entered)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The existing filter error message is retained unchanged; no navigation message or informational action message is set; the error message is displayed on screen as-is

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Existing Filter Error Message Without Override
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account or card filter validation errors exist, the system preserves the existing filter error message and does not replace it with any navigation or informational message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen and is currently on the first page of results
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 (Previous Page) to navigate backward
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message is set to 'NO PREVIOUS PAGES TO DISPLAY' and this message is displayed on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display No Previous Pages Message When Navigating Before First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user attempts to navigate to a previous page while already on the first page of the card list, the system informs them that no earlier pages are available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen, there are no more card records beyond the current page, and the last page has already been shown to the user in a previous interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 (Next Page) to navigate forward
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message is set to 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY' and this message is displayed on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display No More Pages Message When Last Page Was Already Shown
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user attempts to navigate forward past the last page of the card list, and the last page has already been displayed in a prior navigation, the system informs them that no further pages exist.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen and there are no more card records beyond the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 (Next Page) and this is the first time the last page is being reached (last page has not yet been marked as shown)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to action instructions (guiding the user to type S for card detail or U to update); the last page status is marked as 'now shown' so that a subsequent PF8 press will display 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY' instead

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Action Instructions When Reaching Last Page for the First Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user navigates forward and reaches the last page of card records for the first time, the system displays action instructions and marks the last page as having been shown so subsequent PF8 presses produce a different message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen with card records displayed, and no filter errors or navigation boundary errors have been triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either no informational message has been set for the current display, or there are additional pages of card records available beyond the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is set to action instructions guiding the user to type S to view card detail or U to update a card

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Action Instructions When Records Are Available and More Pages Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When card records are displayed on screen and either no informational message has been set yet or additional pages of records exist, the system displays action instructions to guide the user on how to interact with the listed cards.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen and none of the specific message trigger conditions are active (no filter errors, not on first page with PF7, not at last page with PF8, no next page flag, and no existing info message)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message setup process evaluates all conditions and none match the defined scenarios
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message is cleared and no informational message is displayed on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Informational Message When No Applicable Condition Is Met
all_rules.Rule_Description: When none of the specific message conditions apply (no filter errors, no navigation boundary reached, no next page indicator, and no active informational message), the system clears the informational message area so no misleading message is shown.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The message setup process has completed evaluating all conditions and an error message value has been set (either from filter validation, navigation boundary, or retained from prior state)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message content is moved to the screen error message display field (ERRMSGO) so it is visible to the user on the Card List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error Message on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all message conditions have been evaluated and the appropriate error message has been determined, the system places the error message into the screen output area for display to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List screen is being prepared for display with card records present
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An informational message is active (not in the 'no info message' state) AND the screen is not in a 'no records found' state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message text is moved to the screen informational message display field (INFOMSGO) and the message color attribute is set to neutral (non-highlighted, non-error color) so the user can distinguish it from error messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Informational Action Message in Neutral Color When Records Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an informational action message has been set and records have been found (not a no-records-found condition), the system displays the informational message in a neutral (non-error) color to distinguish it from error messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is ready to display the credit card list screen to the user, and all card data rows, filter values, field attributes, and messages have been assembled into the screen output area (CCRDLIAO)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the screen transmission sequence by executing all preparation steps: screen header initialization, card data row population, row field attribute setup, filter field attribute setup, and message setup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transmits the fully populated credit card list screen to the user's terminal using the designated map (LIT-THISMAP) and mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET), ensuring all header information, card records, field attributes, and messages are included in the transmission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare and Transmit Fully Populated Credit Card List Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transmitting the screen to the user, the system must complete all screen preparation steps in sequence: initialize screen header fields, populate card data rows, set field attributes, configure filter field attributes, and set informational or error messages. Only after all preparation steps are complete is the screen transmitted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen output area (CCRDLIAO) is fully populated with card data, header information, field attributes, and messages, and the cursor position has been set during screen attribute setup (e.g., ACCTSIDL set to -1 for account filter field, or CARDSIDL set to -1 for card filter field, or a selection field length set to -1 for an error row)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the screen to the user's terminal using the CICS SEND MAP command with the CURSOR option
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is transmitted with the cursor automatically positioned at the field whose length attribute was set to -1 during attribute setup, directing the user to the appropriate input field (invalid filter field, error selection field, or default entry field)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Credit Card List Screen with Cursor Positioned at Appropriate Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: When transmitting the credit card list screen, the system must position the cursor at the field designated during screen attribute setup (e.g., the first invalid field, the account filter field, or the first available selection field), so the user's attention is directed to the most relevant input area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user's terminal currently displays a previous version of the credit card list screen or any other prior screen content
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system transmits the updated credit card list screen to the terminal using the CICS SEND MAP command with the ERASE option
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All previous screen content on the user's terminal is completely cleared before the new credit card list screen is rendered, ensuring the user sees only the current, fully refreshed screen data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Erase Previous Screen Content on Transmission
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each time the credit card list screen is sent to the user's terminal, the previous screen content must be completely erased so the user sees a clean, fully refreshed display. This prevents residual data from a prior screen from being visible alongside the new screen content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen has been successfully transmitted to the user's terminal and the keyboard is currently locked during the transmission process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS SEND MAP command completes the screen transmission with the FREEKB option specified
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The user's keyboard is unlocked and made available for input, allowing the user to enter account filter values, card number filter values, row selection codes (S or U), or press function keys (ENTER, PF3, PF7, PF8) to interact with the displayed credit card list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unlock User Keyboard After Screen Transmission
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the credit card list screen has been transmitted to the user's terminal, the keyboard must be unlocked (freed) so the user can immediately begin entering input such as filter values, row selections, or function key commands. The keyboard remains locked during screen transmission to prevent premature input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen has been fully transmitted to the user's terminal with the cursor positioned, previous content erased, and keyboard unlocked, and the system has completed all screen preparation and transmission steps
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the COMMON-RETURN routine after screen transmission, saving the current communication area (including transaction ID set to LIT-THISTRANID, program name set to LIT-THISPGM, last mapset set to LIT-THISMAPSET, last map set to LIT-THISMAP, and the full program communication area including page number, first card bookmark, last card bookmark, and page state flags) into the return communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is returned to CICS with the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) and the preserved communication area (WS-COMMAREA containing both CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), and the system waits for the user to submit a new request before resuming processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Await User Response After Screen Transmission Complete
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the credit card list screen has been transmitted, the keyboard unlocked, and the screen erased and refreshed, the system returns control to CICS with the current transaction ID and the full communication area, suspending processing until the user submits a response. The session state (page position, filter values, bookmarks) is preserved in the communication area for the next interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen is active and the user has interacted with the screen by entering data and pressing a key to submit
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the screen submission from the credit card list screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system receives all user-entered data from the credit card list screen into the internal input area (CCRDLIAI), making all entered values available for further processing including account ID filter, card number filter, and all 7 row selection indicators

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive Credit Card List Screen Data from Terminal
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits the credit card list screen, the system must receive and capture all data entered by the user from the terminal into the internal working storage for subsequent processing and validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen data has been received from the terminal and the internal input area contains all user-entered values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the account ID filter field from the received screen data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account ID value entered by the user in the account ID filter field on the screen is stored in the internal Account ID field (CC-ACCT-ID), which will be used to filter the displayed card records to only those belonging to the specified account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Account ID Filter Value from Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen data, the system must extract the account ID filter value entered by the user and store it in the designated account ID working storage field for use in filtering the card list results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen data has been received from the terminal and the internal input area contains all user-entered values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the card number filter field from the received screen data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card number value entered by the user in the card number filter field on the screen is stored in the internal Card Number field (CC-CARD-NUM), which will be used to filter the displayed card records to only those matching the specified card number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Card Number Filter Value from Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen data, the system must extract the card number filter value entered by the user and store it in the designated card number working storage field for use in filtering the card list results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen data has been received from the terminal and the internal input area contains all user-entered values including any action code typed in the selection field of row 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the selection indicator field for card row 1 from the received screen data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The action code value entered by the user in the selection field of card row 1 is stored in the Row 1 selection indicator field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(1)), which will be validated to determine if the user intends to view ('S') or update ('U') the card in row 1, or has left it blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Row 1 Card Selection Action Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen data, the system must extract the action code entered by the user in the selection field of card list row 1 and store it for subsequent validation and action routing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen data has been received from the terminal and the internal input area contains all user-entered values including any action code typed in the selection field of row 2
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the selection indicator field for card row 2 from the received screen data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The action code value entered by the user in the selection field of card row 2 is stored in the Row 2 selection indicator field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(2)), which will be validated to determine if the user intends to view ('S') or update ('U') the card in row 2, or has left it blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Row 2 Card Selection Action Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen data, the system must extract the action code entered by the user in the selection field of card list row 2 and store it for subsequent validation and action routing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen data has been received from the terminal and the internal input area contains all user-entered values including any action code typed in the selection field of row 3
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the selection indicator field for card row 3 from the received screen data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The action code value entered by the user in the selection field of card row 3 is stored in the Row 3 selection indicator field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(3)), which will be validated to determine if the user intends to view ('S') or update ('U') the card in row 3, or has left it blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Row 3 Card Selection Action Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen data, the system must extract the action code entered by the user in the selection field of card list row 3 and store it for subsequent validation and action routing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen data has been received from the terminal and the internal input area contains all user-entered values including any action code typed in the selection field of row 4
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the selection indicator field for card row 4 from the received screen data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The action code value entered by the user in the selection field of card row 4 is stored in the Row 4 selection indicator field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(4)), which will be validated to determine if the user intends to view ('S') or update ('U') the card in row 4, or has left it blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Row 4 Card Selection Action Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen data, the system must extract the action code entered by the user in the selection field of card list row 4 and store it for subsequent validation and action routing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen data has been received from the terminal and the internal input area contains all user-entered values including any action code typed in the selection field of row 5
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the selection indicator field for card row 5 from the received screen data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The action code value entered by the user in the selection field of card row 5 is stored in the Row 5 selection indicator field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(5)), which will be validated to determine if the user intends to view ('S') or update ('U') the card in row 5, or has left it blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Row 5 Card Selection Action Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen data, the system must extract the action code entered by the user in the selection field of card list row 5 and store it for subsequent validation and action routing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen data has been received from the terminal and the internal input area contains all user-entered values including any action code typed in the selection field of row 6
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the selection indicator field for card row 6 from the received screen data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The action code value entered by the user in the selection field of card row 6 is stored in the Row 6 selection indicator field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(6)), which will be validated to determine if the user intends to view ('S') or update ('U') the card in row 6, or has left it blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Row 6 Card Selection Action Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen data, the system must extract the action code entered by the user in the selection field of card list row 6 and store it for subsequent validation and action routing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The credit card list screen data has been received from the terminal and the internal input area contains all user-entered values including any action code typed in the selection field of row 7
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the selection indicator field for card row 7 from the received screen data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The action code value entered by the user in the selection field of card row 7 is stored in the Row 7 selection indicator field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(7)), which will be validated to determine if the user intends to view ('S') or update ('U') the card in row 7, or has left it blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Row 7 Card Selection Action Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: After receiving the screen data, the system must extract the action code entered by the user in the selection field of card list row 7 and store it for subsequent validation and action routing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Card List screen and the Account ID filter field is available for input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen with the Account ID filter field left blank (empty), containing only spaces, or entered as zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system treats the account filter as not applied, clears the stored Account ID filter value to zero, sets the account filter status to 'blank/no filter', and continues processing without restricting card records by account ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Filter Treated as Not Applied When Blank or Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID search filter field is left blank, contains only spaces, or is entered as zero, the system treats this as the user not wishing to filter by account, clears any previously stored account filter value, and proceeds without restricting card records by account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Card List screen and has entered a value in the Account ID filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Account ID filter value contains one or more non-numeric characters (i.e., is not a purely numeric value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system: (1) marks the overall input state as an error, (2) marks the account filter status as invalid/not-OK, (3) sets the error message to 'ACCOUNT FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 11 DIGIT NUMBER', (4) clears the stored Account ID filter value to zero, and (5) protects all card selection rows so no card row action can be selected while the error exists

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Filter Rejected When Non-Numeric Characters Entered
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID filter field contains a value that includes non-numeric characters, the system rejects the input, marks the overall input state as invalid, clears the account filter value, and prevents the user from selecting any card rows until the error is corrected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID filter field has been validated and found to contain an invalid (non-numeric) value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card List screen is being prepared for display after an account filter validation error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the Account ID filter field highlighted in red and positions the screen cursor directly to the Account ID filter field so the user can immediately correct the invalid entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Filter Error Field Highlighted in Red with Cursor Positioned
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID filter field has been flagged as invalid, the system visually highlights the Account ID field in red on the screen and positions the cursor to that field to direct the user's attention to the error requiring correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID filter field has been validated and found to contain an invalid (non-numeric) value, setting the 'protect selection rows' flag to active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card List screen is being prepared for display with the account filter error condition active
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All seven card row selection fields (rows 1 through 7) are set to protected/non-enterable mode regardless of whether those rows contain card data, preventing any view or update action on any card row until the account filter error is resolved

all_rules.Rule_Name: All Card Selection Rows Protected When Account Filter Is Invalid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID filter validation fails, all seven card row selection fields on the screen are made non-enterable (protected), preventing the user from attempting to view or update any card while the filter input error exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Card List screen and has entered a value in the Account ID filter field that is not blank, not spaces, and not zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered Account ID filter value consists entirely of numeric digits (passes numeric validation)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system accepts the value as a valid account filter, stores the entered Account ID as the active account filter value to be used when reading card records, and sets the account filter status to 'valid/active', enabling filtering of the card list to show only cards belonging to the specified account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Valid Numeric Account Filter Accepted and Stored as Active Filter
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID filter field contains a value that is entirely numeric, the system accepts it as a valid account filter, stores it as the active account filter for restricting the card list, and marks the account filter status as valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Card List screen and has submitted the screen with the card number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card number filter field is blank (empty or spaces) OR contains a zero value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the card number filter status to 'Blank' (no filter active), clears the card number filter value to zero, and proceeds without applying any card number restriction to the card list results

all_rules.Rule_Name: Blank or Zero Card Number Treated as No Filter
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number search field is left empty or contains only zeros, the system treats this as the user not wishing to filter by card number. No card number filter is applied, and the card number filter status is set to blank so all cards remain eligible for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Card List screen and has submitted the screen with a non-blank, non-zero value in the card number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered card number filter value is not numeric (contains letters, special characters, or other non-numeric content)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system: (1) sets the overall input status to 'Error', (2) sets the card number filter status to 'Not OK' (invalid), (3) protects all card selection rows so no card can be selected, (4) clears the card number filter value to zero, and (5) if no prior error message has already been set, displays the error message: 'CARD ID FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 16 DIGIT NUMBER'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Non-Numeric Card Number Filter Rejected with Validation Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a card number filter value that contains non-numeric characters, the system rejects the input, flags it as an error, prevents any card row from being selected, and clears the card number filter. This enforces that the card number filter must be a valid 16-digit numeric value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card number filter has been determined to be non-numeric and an error condition is being raised
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to set the card number filter error message 'CARD ID FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 16 DIGIT NUMBER'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message is only set if no prior error message has already been recorded (i.e., the error message field is currently in its 'off' or empty state); if a prior error message already exists, the card filter error message is NOT written and the existing error message is preserved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Filter Error Message Set Only When No Prior Error Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a non-numeric card number filter triggers an error, the specific card filter error message is only written if no other error message has already been recorded during the current validation cycle. This ensures the first error encountered takes precedence and is not overwritten by subsequent validation errors.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Card List screen and has submitted the screen with a non-blank, non-zero value in the card number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered card number filter value is numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stores the numeric card number value as the active card number filter, sets the card number filter status to 'Valid', and the card list will subsequently be filtered to display only cards whose card number matches the entered value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Valid Numeric Card Number Accepted as Active Card Filter
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a card number filter value that is numeric and non-zero, the system accepts it as a valid active filter. The numeric card number value is stored as the active card filter, and the filter status is marked as valid so that subsequent card list reads will restrict results to only cards matching this card number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Card List screen and either the Account ID filter or the Card Number filter has already been flagged as invalid (INPUT-ERROR is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to perform row selection validation on the 7 card selection fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system immediately skips all row selection validation steps and exits the validation routine without evaluating any of the 7 row selection codes, leaving all row-level error indicators unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Row Selection Validation When Prior Input Errors Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account or card filter validation has already failed before row selection validation begins, the system bypasses all row selection checks entirely to avoid redundant or misleading error messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: No prior input errors exist and the system is proceeding with row selection validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system inspects the combined selection flags field (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS) which concatenates all 7 row selection entries
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system tallies the total count of all occurrences of 'S' (View) and 'U' (Update) values across all 7 row selection fields and stores the total count in the counter variable I for use in the multiple-selection check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Count Total Row Selections Across All Seven Card Rows
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before evaluating individual row selections, the system counts the total number of action codes entered across all 7 card rows to determine whether the user has attempted to act on more than one card simultaneously.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has counted the total number of 'S' and 'U' entries across all 7 card rows and the total count is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The multiple-selection count check is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the overall input status to error (INPUT-ERROR), activates the multiple-selection error flag (WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION), copies the combined selection flags into the error flags field (WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS), and replaces every 'S' and 'U' in the error flags with '1' and every other character with '0', thereby marking exactly those rows that contained a selection code as rows in error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Submission When More Than One Card Row Is Selected
all_rules.Rule_Description: A user is only permitted to act on one card at a time. If the user enters a selection code ('S' or 'U') in more than one row simultaneously, the system rejects the submission and marks every selected row as being in error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed the multiple-selection count check (regardless of whether a multiple-selection error was found or not) and is about to begin row-by-row evaluation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the selected row tracking variable
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The selected row index variable (I-SELECTED) is set to zero, indicating that no row has yet been identified as the user's intended selection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Selected Row Index Before Row-by-Row Evaluation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before iterating through the 7 card rows to identify which row the user selected, the system resets the selected row index to zero to ensure no stale value from a prior screen interaction is carried forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through card rows 1 to 7 and the current row's selection field contains either 'S' (View) or 'U' (Update), which are the only two valid action codes
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection code for the current row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current row number (1 through 7) into the selected row index variable (I-SELECTED), making it available for the downstream action routing logic to determine which card's Account Number and Card Number to pass to the next screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record the Index of a Valid Single Row Selection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card row contains a valid action code ('S' for View or 'U' for Update), the system records that row's position number so that the subsequent action (navigate to Card Detail or Card Update) can be directed to the correct card.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through card rows 1 to 7, the current row contains a valid selection code ('S' or 'U'), and the multiple-selection error flag (WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION) is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether a multiple-selection error is in effect for this valid row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the row-level error indicator for the current row (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR(I)) to '1', causing that row's selection field to be highlighted in red on the screen to alert the user that this row is part of an invalid multiple-selection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark a Valid Selection Row as Error When Multiple Selections Were Made
all_rules.Rule_Description: Even though a row contains a technically valid action code ('S' or 'U'), if the user selected more than one row simultaneously, each individually valid selection must also be flagged as an error to visually indicate to the user which rows caused the conflict.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through card rows 1 to 7 and the current row's selection field is blank (SELECT-BLANK condition is true, meaning the field contains spaces or low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection code for the current row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system takes no action for that row, does not set any error indicator, does not update the selected row index, and proceeds to evaluate the next row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept Blank Row Selection as No Action Required
all_rules.Rule_Description: A card row where the user has left the selection field blank or empty is considered a deliberate non-selection and requires no validation action. The system silently skips such rows.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through card rows 1 to 7 and the current row's selection field contains a value that is neither 'S' (View), 'U' (Update), nor blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection code for the current row and finds it does not match any valid code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the overall input status to error (INPUT-ERROR), sets the row-level error indicator for the current row (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR(I)) to '1' to trigger red highlighting on that row's selection field, and if no prior error message has been set, activates the invalid action code error message (WS-INVALID-ACTION-CODE) to inform the user that only 'S' or 'U' are accepted selection values

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject and Flag an Invalid Action Code Entered in a Card Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: If a user enters any value other than 'S', 'U', or blank in a card row's selection field, the system treats it as an unrecognized action code, marks that row as invalid, and sets an error message to inform the user of the correct valid values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward card read operation is about to begin for a new page of results
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the forward read process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 7 card display rows are cleared to empty values, the screen row counter is set to zero, and the Next Page Exists indicator is set to true in preparation for reading

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Screen Rows and Initialize Page State Before Forward Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before reading card records forward, all display rows must be cleared and the row counter reset to zero so that stale data from a previous page is not shown to the user. The next-page indicator is optimistically set to 'exists' at the start.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A starting card number key (WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM) has been set for the forward read
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates a browse of the Card File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file browse is positioned at the first card record whose card number is greater than or equal to the starting card number key, so that subsequent reads proceed forward from that position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Position Card File Browse at or After Starting Card Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: The card file browse must be positioned at the record whose card number is greater than or equal to the provided starting card number key, ensuring the forward read begins at the correct position in the file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A browse of the Card File has been started and the read loop is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the next card record sequentially from the Card File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A card record containing Card Number, Account ID, and Active Status is retrieved; if the end of the file is reached, the end-of-file condition is flagged; if a normal or duplicate record response is received, the record is available for filter evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Card Record Sequentially from Card File
all_rules.Rule_Description: During the forward browse loop, the system reads the next sequential card record from the Card File. The outcome determines whether a valid record was found, the end of file was reached, or another condition occurred.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully read from the Card File and an Account ID filter has been validated and is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the card record's Account ID matches the Account ID filter value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the card record's Account ID equals the filter Account ID, the record passes the account filter and proceeds to card number filter evaluation; if the card record's Account ID does not match, the record is excluded from the display and the system reads the next record without incrementing the row counter

all_rules.Rule_Name: Filter Card Records by Account ID When Account Filter Is Active
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user has supplied a valid Account ID as a filter, only card records whose Account ID exactly matches the filter value should be included in the display. Records with a non-matching Account ID are excluded and the next record is read.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has passed the Account ID filter check and a Card Number filter has been validated and is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the card record's Card Number matches the Card Number filter value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the card record's Card Number equals the filter Card Number, the record passes the card number filter and is included in the display; if the card record's Card Number does not match, the record is excluded from the display and the system reads the next record without incrementing the row counter

all_rules.Rule_Name: Filter Card Records by Card Number When Card Number Filter Is Active
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user has supplied a valid Card Number as a filter, only card records whose Card Number exactly matches the filter value should be included in the display. Records with a non-matching Card Number are excluded and the next record is read.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has passed all active filter checks (Account ID filter and Card Number filter)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the qualifying card record in the display list
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card's Card Number, Account ID, and Active Status are stored in the next available screen row position (indexed by the row counter), and the row counter is incremented by 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Qualifying Card Record Data in Screen Display Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each card record that passes all active filters is stored in the next available screen display row. The row counter is incremented to track how many qualifying records have been collected for the current page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has just been stored as the first qualifying record on the current page (row counter equals 1)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system identifies this as the first qualifying record for the page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card's Account ID is saved as the First Card Account ID bookmark and the card's Card Number is saved as the First Card Number bookmark for page-up navigation; additionally, if the current screen page number is zero, it is incremented by 1 to set the page number to 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save First Qualifying Card as Page-Up Navigation Bookmark
all_rules.Rule_Description: The first qualifying card record on a page must be saved as the navigation bookmark so that the system can navigate back to the beginning of this page when the user presses PF7 (page up). If the page number has not yet been set, it is initialized to 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Card records are being read and stored in screen display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row counter reaches the maximum of 7 rows (WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The read loop is flagged to exit, and the current card's Account ID and Card Number are saved as the Last Card Account ID and Last Card Number bookmarks respectively, to be used as the starting position for the next page-down navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Reading When Page Is Full and Save Last Card Navigation Bookmark
all_rules.Rule_Description: When 7 qualifying card records have been collected, the current page is full. The system saves the last card's details as the navigation bookmark for page-down (PF8) navigation and stops the read loop to proceed with checking for additional records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current page has been filled with 7 qualifying card records and the last card bookmark has been saved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads one additional record from the Card File beyond the last displayed record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If an additional record is found (normal or duplicate response), the Next Page Exists indicator is set to true and the Last Card Account ID and Last Card Number bookmarks are updated to this additional record's values; if the end of file is reached, the Next Page Not Exists indicator is set to true and the message 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW' is set (only if no prior error message exists)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Peek Ahead to Determine If a Next Page of Records Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: After filling a full page of 7 records, the system reads one additional record to determine whether more records exist beyond the current page. This controls whether the PF8 (next page) navigation option is available to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is reading card records in the forward read loop and has not yet filled all 7 display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end of the Card File is reached (no more records to read)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The read loop is flagged to exit, the Next Page Not Exists indicator is set to true, the last read card's Account ID and Card Number are saved as the Last Card Account ID and Last Card Number bookmarks, and the message 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW' is set if no prior error message has already been set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle End of Card File During Forward Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the card file is reached during the main forward read loop (before filling 7 rows), the system marks that no next page exists, saves the last read card details as the Last Card bookmark, and sets an informational message for the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The end of the Card File has been reached during a forward read
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current screen page number is 1 (first page) AND the screen row counter is zero (no qualifying records were found)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The No Records Found indicator is set to true, which will suppress normal informational messages and display a 'no records found' notification to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set No Records Found Indicator When First Page Returns Zero Results
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system is on the first page of results and the end of file is reached without finding any qualifying records, a specific 'No Records Found' indicator is set to inform the user that no cards match the applied filters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The forward card read loop has completed for any reason (page full, end of file, or error)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the forward read operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card File browse session is ended, releasing the file browse position and completing the forward read process

all_rules.Rule_Name: End Card File Browse After Forward Read Completes
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the forward read loop has completed (either by filling 7 rows, reaching end of file, or encountering an error), the card file browse session must be formally closed to release file resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is reading card records forward from the card file and adding qualifying records to the current page display list
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of records added to the current page display equals the maximum allowed records per page (7)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stops adding records to the current page, records the last card's Account ID and Card Number as the Last Card Key bookmark for the current page, and proceeds to perform a peek-ahead read to determine if more records exist beyond the current page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect When a Full Page of Card Records Has Been Filled
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each card record is added to the display list during a forward read, the system checks whether the maximum number of records per page (7) has been reached to determine if a next-page existence check should be triggered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current page has been filled with exactly 7 card records and the system is about to check whether more records exist
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The page-full condition is confirmed (record count equals 7)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system saves the Account ID of the 7th (last) card record into the Last Card Account ID bookmark (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-ACCT-ID) and saves the Card Number of the 7th (last) card record into the Last Card Number bookmark (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-NUM), so that these values can be used as the starting point for the next page navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record the Last Card Key of the Current Page Before Peek-Ahead
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before attempting to read beyond the current page, the system saves the Account ID and Card Number of the last record displayed on the current page. These values serve as navigation bookmarks enabling forward and backward pagination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current page has been filled with 7 card records and the Last Card Key bookmark has been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a peek-ahead read by attempting to read the next sequential record from the card file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system evaluates the outcome of this read attempt — either a record is found (indicating more pages exist) or the end of the card file is reached (indicating the current page is the last page) — and updates the next-page indicator accordingly

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attempt to Read One Additional Record Beyond the Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After filling a full page of 7 records and recording the last card key, the system performs a single additional sequential read from the card file to determine whether any records exist beyond the current page, without displaying that record to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a peek-ahead read after filling the current page with 7 records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The peek-ahead read returns a valid card record (read is successful — normal or duplicate record response)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the next-page indicator as 'Next Page EXISTS' (enabling the Page Down / PF8 navigation option for the user), and updates the Last Card Account ID bookmark with the peeked record's Account ID and updates the Last Card Number bookmark with the peeked record's Card Number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Next Page as Existing and Update Last Card Key When More Records Are Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the peek-ahead read successfully retrieves a record beyond the current page, the system confirms that a next page is available for navigation and updates the Last Card Key bookmark with the peeked record's details to ensure accurate forward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a peek-ahead read after filling the current page with 7 records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The peek-ahead read reaches the end of the card file (no more records exist beyond the current page)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the next-page indicator as 'Next Page DOES NOT EXIST' (disabling the Page Down / PF8 navigation option), and if no prior error message has already been set, displays the informational message 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW' to inform the user that the current page is the last available page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Next Page as Not Existing When End of Card File Is Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the peek-ahead read reaches the end of the card file, the system confirms that the user is viewing the last available page of card records and sets an informational message to notify the user that no further records are available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is in the forward read loop and is adding qualifying card records to the current page display list
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of records added to the current page is less than the maximum records per page (fewer than 7 records)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not trigger the next-page existence check, does not record the Last Card Key bookmark, and continues reading the next sequential record from the card file to attempt to fill the remaining slots on the current page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Reading Records When Current Page Is Not Yet Full
all_rules.Rule_Description: While the number of qualifying card records added to the current page display is less than the maximum of 7, the system continues reading the next sequential record from the card file without triggering the next-page existence check.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has requested to navigate to the previous page of the card list
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward card record reading process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 7 screen display rows (Account Number, Card Number, Card Active Status, and Selection fields) are cleared to empty/low values before any new records are loaded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Screen Rows Before Backward Page Load
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before reading the previous page of card records, all existing screen display rows must be cleared to ensure no stale data from the prior page remains visible to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current page is displaying card records and the first card key (WS-CA-FIRST-CARDKEY) is known
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward card record reading process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current first card key is copied to the last card key field (WS-CA-LAST-CARDKEY) and used as the starting position (RIDFLD) for opening the backward browse on the card file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Current First Card Key as Backward Browse Starting Point
all_rules.Rule_Description: The card number of the first record currently displayed on screen must be saved and used as the starting position for the backward file browse, ensuring the system navigates backward from the correct position in the card file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward browse starting point has been set to the current page's first card key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card file browse is opened for backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card file browse is started at the position of the current first card key using GTEQ positioning, so that backward reads will retrieve records preceding the current page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Backward Browse on Card File from First Card Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: The card file browse must be opened at or after the current page's first card key position using a greater-than-or-equal (GTEQ) positioning, enabling subsequent backward reads to retrieve the preceding page of records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card file backward browse has been successfully opened
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen position counter is initialized for backward page filling
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen position counter (WS-SCRN-COUNTER) is set to WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES + 1 (value of 8), so that after skipping the first record and decrementing, the first qualifying record is placed in the bottom-most display row (row 7) and subsequent records fill upward toward row 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Screen Position Counter to Bottom of Screen for Upward Fill
all_rules.Rule_Description: Because records are read in reverse order (newest-to-oldest), the screen array must be filled from the bottom row upward. The screen position counter is initialized to one position beyond the maximum screen lines (7+1=8) so that after the first skip-read decrement it starts at row 7 and fills upward to row 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward browse has been opened at the current page's first card key position
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first backward read is performed immediately after opening the browse
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the read is successful (NORMAL or DUPREC response), the screen position counter is decremented by 1 (from 8 to 7) and the record data is discarded — this record is the current page's first record and must not appear on the previous page. If the read fails with any other response, the backward reading process is terminated with an error.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip First Record Read to Exclude Current Page's First Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The first backward read after opening the browse returns the current page's first record, which is already displayed and should not be included in the previous page. This record must be skipped, and the screen position counter decremented to align with the correct starting row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward browse is open and the screen position counter is greater than 0
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A backward read is performed in the read loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the previous card record from the card file into the CARD-RECORD area, capturing Card Number, Account ID, and Card Active Status for potential display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Previous Card Record from Card File in Backward Direction
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each iteration of the backward read loop retrieves the next preceding card record from the card file, moving backward through the file to populate the previous page of the card list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A backward read has been performed on the card file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read response is anything other than NORMAL or DUPREC (e.g., beginning of file or file error)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The read loop is immediately exited, the operation name 'READ' and the card file name are recorded in the error context fields, and the file error message is set in WS-ERROR-MSG for display to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Unsuccessful Backward Record Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a backward read returns an unexpected result (not a normal read or duplicate record), the backward reading loop must be terminated to prevent further processing on an invalid file state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A backward card record read has returned a valid record AND an account number filter is active (FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account filter check is applied to the retrieved card record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the card record's Account ID (CARD-ACCT-ID) matches the filter Account ID (CC-ACCT-ID), the record is retained for potential display. If the card record's Account ID does NOT match the filter Account ID, the record is excluded and the next record is read without placing this record on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Account Number Filter During Backward Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account number filter has been entered by the user, each card record read during backward navigation must be checked to ensure its account ID matches the filter value. Records belonging to a different account must be excluded from the display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A backward card record read has returned a valid record AND a card number filter is active (FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card number filter check is applied to the retrieved card record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the card record's Card Number (CARD-NUM) matches the filter Card Number (CC-CARD-NUM-N), the record is retained for potential display. If the card record's Card Number does NOT match the filter Card Number, the record is excluded and the next record is read without placing this record on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Card Number Filter During Backward Read
