all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card number filter has been entered by the user, each card record read during backward navigation must be checked to ensure its card number matches the filter value. Records with a different card number must be excluded from the display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A backward card record read has returned a valid record AND both an account number filter (FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID) and a card number filter (FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID) are active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Both filters are applied sequentially to the retrieved card record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record is included in the display only if CARD-ACCT-ID matches CC-ACCT-ID AND CARD-NUM matches CC-CARD-NUM-N. If either condition fails, the record is excluded and the system reads the next record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Combined Account and Card Number Filters During Backward Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When both an account number filter and a card number filter are active simultaneously, a card record must satisfy BOTH filter conditions to be included in the display. Failing either filter results in the record being excluded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has been read successfully and has passed all active filter checks (account and/or card number filters)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record is accepted for display on the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card's Card Number (CARD-NUM) is stored in WS-ROW-CARD-NUM at the current screen counter position, the card's Account ID (CARD-ACCT-ID) is stored in WS-ROW-ACCTNO at the current screen counter position, and the card's Active Status (CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS) is stored in WS-ROW-CARD-STATUS at the current screen counter position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place Qualifying Record in Current Screen Row During Backward Fill
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each card record that passes all active filters is placed into the current screen row position, storing the Account Number, Card Number, and Card Active Status for display to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A qualifying card record has been successfully placed into the current screen row (WS-SCRN-COUNTER position)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen row placement is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen position counter (WS-SCRN-COUNTER) is decremented by 1, moving the next available fill position one row upward on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Move Screen Position Up One Row After Placing Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: After placing a qualifying record into the current screen row, the screen position counter must be decremented by 1 to move the fill position upward toward row 1, maintaining the correct top-to-bottom display order for records that were read in reverse.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A qualifying card record has been placed in a screen row and the screen position counter has been decremented
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen position counter (WS-SCRN-COUNTER) is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If WS-SCRN-COUNTER equals 0, all 7 screen rows have been filled — the read loop is flagged to exit (READ-LOOP-EXIT set to TRUE) and the first card key bookmark is updated. If WS-SCRN-COUNTER is greater than 0, the loop continues reading the next previous record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect When Previous Page is Fully Populated with 7 Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each record is placed and the screen position counter is decremented, the system must check whether all 7 screen rows have been filled. When the counter reaches 0, the previous page is complete and the read loop must stop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen position counter has reached 0, indicating all 7 rows of the previous page have been filled
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read loop exit condition is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID of the current card record (CARD-ACCT-ID) is saved to WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-ACCT-ID and the Card Number of the current card record (CARD-NUM) is saved to WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM, establishing this record as the new starting point for the now-displayed previous page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update First Card Key Bookmark to New Page's First Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the previous page has been fully populated with 7 records, the card number and account ID of the last record placed (which is the topmost record on the new page) must be saved as the new first card key bookmark. This bookmark is used for future navigation — both for further backward navigation and for re-reading this page forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward card record reading loop has ended for any reason (page full, beginning of file reached, or error encountered)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read process concludes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card file browse is closed (ENDBR issued on the card file), and the previous page data is ready for screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Card File Browse After Backward Read Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the backward read loop has completed — whether because 7 records were collected, no more records exist, or an error occurred — the card file browse must be closed to release file resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved from the card file during a forward or backward browse operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins evaluating whether the record should be displayed on the card list screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record is marked as INCLUDED by default, meaning it is considered eligible for display unless a subsequent active filter condition explicitly excludes it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Record Inclusion Before Filter Evaluation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any filter criteria are evaluated, every card record retrieved during a browse operation is initially marked as eligible for display. This default-include stance ensures that records are only excluded when a specific active filter condition explicitly disqualifies them.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has been retrieved and marked as INCLUDED by default, and the user may or may not have entered an Account ID in the account filter field on the card list screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the account filter flag is set to valid (indicating the user supplied a valid numeric Account ID as a filter)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account filter is active (flag is valid), the system proceeds to compare the card record's Account ID against the filter value; if the account filter is not active, the system skips the account ID comparison and proceeds directly to evaluate the card number filter

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Filter Active Status Determination
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system determines whether an account filter has been applied by the user. An account filter is considered active only when the user has entered a valid numeric Account ID in the account filter field on the card list screen. If no account filter is active, the account ID of the card record is not evaluated and the record proceeds to the card number filter check.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account filter is active with a valid numeric Account ID entered by the user, and a card record has been retrieved from the card file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the card record's Account ID field against the user-supplied Account ID filter value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the card record's Account ID exactly matches the filter value, the record remains INCLUDED and the system proceeds to evaluate the card number filter; if the card record's Account ID does not match the filter value, the record is immediately marked as EXCLUDED and no further filter evaluation is performed for that record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account ID Match Evaluation and Exclusion
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account filter is active, the system compares the account ID on the card record against the account ID entered by the user as a filter. If the values do not match, the record is immediately excluded from the display list and no further filter checks are performed for that record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has passed the account filter check (or no account filter was active) and is still marked as INCLUDED, and the user may or may not have entered a Card Number in the card number filter field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the card number filter flag is set to valid (indicating the user supplied a valid numeric Card Number as a filter)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the card number filter is active (flag is valid), the system proceeds to compare the card record's Card Number against the filter value; if the card number filter is not active, the record is confirmed as INCLUDED and passes all filter checks, making it eligible for display on the card list screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Filter Active Status Determination
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system determines whether a card number filter has been applied by the user. A card number filter is considered active only when the user has entered a valid numeric Card Number in the card number filter field on the card list screen. If no card number filter is active, the card number of the record is not evaluated and the record is confirmed as included for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card number filter is active with a valid numeric Card Number entered by the user, and a card record has already passed the account filter check and is still marked as INCLUDED
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the card record's Card Number field against the user-supplied Card Number filter value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the card record's Card Number exactly matches the filter value, the record is confirmed as INCLUDED and passes all active filter checks, making it eligible for display on the card list screen; if the card record's Card Number does not match the filter value, the record is immediately marked as EXCLUDED and is not displayed on the card list screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Match Evaluation and Exclusion
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card number filter is active, the system compares the card number on the card record against the card number entered by the user as a filter. If the values do not match, the record is immediately excluded from the display list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has been retrieved from the card file during browsing, and one or both of the following filters may be active: an Account ID filter and/or a Card Number filter entered by the user on the card list screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the card record against all active filters sequentially — first the account filter (if active), then the card number filter (if active)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record is marked as INCLUDED and displayed on the card list screen only if it passes every active filter check (Account ID matches when account filter is active AND Card Number matches when card number filter is active); if the record fails any single active filter, it is marked as EXCLUDED and is not displayed on the card list screen, with no further filter evaluation performed for that record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Combined Filter Logic - Record Must Pass All Active Filters
all_rules.Rule_Description: A card record is eligible for display on the card list screen only when it satisfies all active filter conditions simultaneously. Both the account filter and the card number filter operate as AND conditions — a record must match every active filter to be included. Records that fail any single active filter are excluded from display regardless of other filter results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program has completed processing a user interaction (any key press or action) and is preparing to return control to CICS to await the next user input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches the session state persistence step (COMMON-RETURN) prior to issuing the CICS RETURN command
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The session context must be updated with: (1) the current transaction ID saved as the 'from transaction ID' field in the application-wide communication area (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), (2) the current program name saved as the 'from program' field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), (3) the current mapset name saved as the 'last mapset' field (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), and (4) the current map name saved as the 'last map' field (CDEMO-LAST-MAP), so that the next program or screen interaction can identify the originating program and map

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program Identity Before Session Handoff
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before returning control to CICS, the Card List program must stamp the session context with its own identity — including the transaction ID, program name, current map name, and current mapset name — so that the next screen interaction knows which program last handled the session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program has completed processing and the application-wide communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) contains the current session's shared data including user type, account ID, card number, program entry/re-entry state, last map, last mapset, and next program routing information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program executes the session state save step in COMMON-RETURN
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire contents of the application-wide communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be copied verbatim into the beginning (first part) of the combined session storage area (WS-COMMAREA), occupying positions 1 through the full length of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, preserving all shared session fields for use by subsequent programs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Application-Wide Session Data as First Part of Combined Storage
all_rules.Rule_Description: The application-wide communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which holds shared session data such as user type, account ID, card number, program entry state, and navigation context, must be copied into the first portion of the combined session storage area (WS-COMMAREA) before returning to CICS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card List program has completed processing and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA contains the program-specific session state including: the first card number bookmark (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM), the last card number bookmark (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-NUM), the first card account ID bookmark (WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-ACCT-ID), the last card account ID bookmark (WS-CA-LAST-CARD-ACCT-ID), the current screen/page number (WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM), pagination indicators (CA-FIRST-PAGE, CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS/NOT-EXISTS, CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN/NOT-SHOWN), and program return flags
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program executes the session state save step in COMMON-RETURN after the application-wide data has been placed in WS-COMMAREA
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire contents of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA must be copied into WS-COMMAREA starting at the position immediately after the end of the application-wide communication area (at offset: LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1) and extending for the full length of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, so that all card list pagination state and navigation bookmarks are preserved for the next screen interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Program-Specific Session Data as Second Part of Combined Storage
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card List program's own session data (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), which includes card key bookmarks for pagination (first and last card numbers and account IDs), the current screen/page number, pagination state indicators (first page flag, next page exists flag, last page shown flag), and program return flags, must be saved into the second portion of the combined session storage area immediately after the application-wide data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The application-wide communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) both contain current, up-to-date session state data after all processing for the current user interaction is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program constructs the combined communication area in COMMON-RETURN
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The combined session storage area (WS-COMMAREA) must be structured as: Segment 1 — positions 1 to LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA contain the full application-wide communication area data; Segment 2 — positions (LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1) to (LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + LENGTH OF WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) contain the full program-specific communication area data; the two segments must be contiguous with no padding or gap between them, forming a single unified block whose total length equals the sum of both individual area lengths

all_rules.Rule_Name: Merge Application-Wide and Program-Specific Data into Single Combined Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: The combined session storage area (WS-COMMAREA) must be constructed as a single contiguous block by placing the application-wide communication area in the first segment and the program-specific communication area in the second segment, with no gap between them, forming one unified communication area ready to be passed to CICS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) has been fully populated with both the application-wide session data and the program-specific session data (card keys, screen number, pagination indicators, return flags), and the program identity fields (transaction ID, program name, map, mapset) have been recorded in the session context
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program issues the CICS RETURN command in COMMON-RETURN
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control must be returned to CICS with: (1) the next transaction ID set to the current program's own transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID), ensuring the same Card List transaction is re-invoked on the next user key press, (2) the combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) passed as the COMMAREA, and (3) the length of the COMMAREA set to the full length of WS-COMMAREA, so that the complete session state — including pagination bookmarks, page number, filter values, and navigation flags — is available when the program is next entered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to CICS with Preserved Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all session state has been saved into the combined communication area, the Card List program must return control to CICS specifying the same transaction ID so that the next user interaction (key press) will re-invoke this same program, and passing the full combined communication area so all session state is available when the program is next entered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward read of the credit card file has been performed, the current page being displayed is Page 1 (screen number equals 1), and the system has reached the end of the card file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of qualifying records found on this page is zero (no records passed the account ID and/or card number filters)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Records Found' indicator to TRUE, signaling that no credit cards match the current search criteria entered by the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect No Matching Credit Cards on First Page Search
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system performs a forward read of credit card records and reaches the end of the card file on the very first page without finding any qualifying records, it must set a 'No Records Found' indicator to signal that no credit cards match the current search criteria (account ID filter and/or card number filter).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing the card list screen for display and has completed reading card records from the file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The 'No Records Found' indicator is set to TRUE (meaning zero qualifying credit card records were found matching the search criteria)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does NOT display the informational action instructions message (the message guiding users to type 'S' for detail or 'U' to update) on the screen, leaving the informational message area blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Suppress Action Instructions When No Records Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the 'No Records Found' indicator is active, the system must suppress the standard informational action instructions message (which normally guides users to type 'S' for card detail or 'U' to update a card). Showing action instructions when there are no records to act upon would be misleading to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a forward read of the credit card file, the current page is Page 1, the end of the card file has been reached, and no qualifying records were found (record count equals zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The 'No Records Found' indicator is TRUE and no prior error message has been set (error message flag is in the OFF/blank state)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error message to 'NO MORE RECORDS TO SHOW', sets the 'No Records Found' indicator, suppresses the informational action instructions message, and displays the card list screen to the user with the error message visible and no card data rows populated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display No Records Found Message to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card file read completes on the first page with zero qualifying records, the system must communicate to the user that no credit cards match their current search criteria. The 'No More Records To Show' message is set as the error message, and the action instructions are suppressed, resulting in a screen that clearly indicates no matching records exist.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a forward read of the credit card file and has reached the end of the card file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current screen number is NOT equal to 1 (the user is on a page beyond the first page of results)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does NOT set the 'No Records Found' indicator regardless of the record count, and the screen is displayed normally with any found records and the standard informational action instructions message visible

all_rules.Rule_Name: Bypass No Records Check When Not on First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: The 'No Records Found' indicator is only evaluated and set when the system is reading the very first page of results. If the system is reading any page other than the first page, the no-records check is not applicable, and the screen proceeds with normal display including action instructions for any records shown.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen and has previously navigated to and viewed the last available page of card records (last page already shown flag is set), and no further pages of card records exist beyond the currently displayed page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Page Down key (PF8) to attempt to navigate to the next page of card records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error message to 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY' and redisplays the Card List screen with this error message, indicating to the user that there are no additional pages of card records to navigate to

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display 'No More Pages' Error When User Attempts to Navigate Beyond Last Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses the Page Down key (PF8) to navigate forward in the card list, but there are no more pages of records available AND the last page has already been displayed to the user in a prior navigation step, the system must inform the user that no additional pages exist by displaying the error message 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY'.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen and has navigated to a page where no additional pages of card records exist beyond the currently displayed page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 (Next Page) and the system determines that no next page of card records exists
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message to 'TYPE S FOR DETAIL, U TO UPDATE' to instruct the user on available row-level actions for the displayed card records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Action Instructions When Last Page Reached via PF8
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 (Next Page) and there are no further pages of card records available, the system displays action instruction message guiding the user on how to interact with the displayed card records — specifically to enter 'S' to view card detail or 'U' to update a card.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen, has pressed PF8, no next page of card records exists, and the last page has NOT yet been previously shown to the user (last-page-not-shown indicator is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the PF8 action and confirms that no next page exists and the last page has not yet been shown
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the last page indicator as 'now shown' (sets CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN to TRUE), so that any subsequent PF8 press will trigger the 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY' message instead of the action instructions message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Last Page as Shown When First Reached via PF8
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 and reaches the last page of card records for the first time, the system updates the last-page-shown indicator so that subsequent PF8 presses can correctly display the 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY' message instead of repeating the action instructions message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the Card List screen, has pressed PF8, no next page of card records exists, and the last page HAS already been shown to the user in a previous interaction (CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN is already TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the last page shown indicator needs to be updated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does NOT update the last-page-shown indicator and exits message setup without any change to the last-page state, allowing the 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY' message to be triggered on the next PF8 press

all_rules.Rule_Name: Suppress Last Page Shown Update When Last Page Already Displayed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 and the last page has already been shown in a prior interaction, the system does not update the last-page-shown indicator again. This preserves the state so that the correct 'NO MORE PAGES TO DISPLAY' message continues to be shown on further PF8 presses.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the card list screen with one or more selection fields filled in across up to 7 card rows, and no prior account or card filter validation errors exist
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system scans the combined selection flag area (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS) representing all 7 row selection fields and counts every occurrence of 'S' (View action) and every occurrence of 'U' (Update action) to produce a total selection count
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system holds the total count of all 'S' and 'U' entries found across all 7 rows in counter variable I, which is then used to determine whether a single or multiple row selection has been made

all_rules.Rule_Name: Count Total Row Selections Across Card List
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits the card list screen, the system scans all 7 row selection fields simultaneously and tallies the total number of View ('S') and Update ('U') action codes entered across all rows to determine how many rows have been selected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed counting all 'S' (View) and 'U' (Update) entries across all 7 card list rows and the total count is held in counter I
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The total count of selected rows (I) is greater than 1, meaning the user has entered action codes in more than one row simultaneously
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the overall input validation state to INPUT-ERROR (marking the entire screen submission as invalid) and sets the WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION flag to TRUE to specifically identify this as a multiple-selection error, distinguishing it from other types of row selection errors

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Multiple Row Selections and Set Error State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The card list screen enforces a business rule that only one card row may be actioned at a time. If a user enters action codes in more than one row, the system must immediately flag the entire submission as invalid and record the specific nature of the error as a multiple-selection violation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that more than one row has been selected (INPUT-ERROR is TRUE and WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system copies the current combined selection flags (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS, containing the raw 'S', 'U', or blank values for all 7 rows) into the error tracking flags area (WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error tracking area (WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS) holds an exact copy of the user's selection entries, ready to be transformed into per-row error indicators in the next step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Selection State for Error Row Identification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a multiple-selection error is detected, the system must preserve a snapshot of which rows were selected so that each individual row can be independently evaluated and marked with an error indicator. This snapshot is copied into a dedicated error tracking area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error tracking area (WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS) contains a copy of the user's row selection entries, with 'S', 'U', or blank values for each of the 7 rows, and a multiple-selection error has been confirmed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the error tracking area by replacing every 'S' character with '1', every 'U' character with '1', and every remaining character (blanks or any other value) with '0'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error tracking area (WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS) contains a binary error map where '1' indicates a row that was incorrectly selected as part of a multiple-selection violation and '0' indicates a row that was not selected, enabling the screen to highlight all offending rows in red during the subsequent display step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Each Selected Row with Error Indicator for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a multiple-selection error is detected, the system must identify precisely which rows the user selected so they can be highlighted in red on the screen. Every row that had a View ('S') or Update ('U') code is marked with error indicator '1', and all other rows are marked with '0' to clearly distinguish erroneous selections from non-selected rows.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Card List screen and prior input validation errors have already been flagged (INPUT-ERROR is TRUE) due to invalid account filter or card number filter entries
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row selection validation routine (2250-EDIT-ARRAY) is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips all row selection validation checks entirely and exits the routine immediately without evaluating any of the 7 row selection fields, preserving the existing error state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Row Selection Validation When Prior Input Errors Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When input errors have already been detected during account or card filter validation, the row selection validation is bypassed entirely to avoid cascading error messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Card List screen with no prior input errors, and the 7 row selection fields (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS, positions 1-7) may contain any combination of 'S', 'U', or other values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row selection validation routine begins counting selections
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system inspects the combined selection flags string (WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS) and tallies the total count (stored in counter variable I) of all occurrences of 'S' (View) and 'U' (Update) codes across all 7 rows, treating both 'S' and 'U' as valid selection indicators for the purpose of counting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Count Total Row Selections Across All Seven Rows
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validating individual row selections, the system tallies the total number of View ('S') and Update ('U') action codes entered across all 7 card list rows to determine if multiple rows have been selected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted the Card List screen and the total count of 'S' and 'U' selections across all 7 rows is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The multiple-selection check is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets INPUT-ERROR to TRUE, sets the WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION flag to TRUE, copies the selection flags into WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS, and replaces every 'S' and 'U' in WS-EDIT-SELECT-ERROR-FLAGS with '1' (error indicator) and all other characters with '0', so that every row that had a selection is individually marked for red highlighting on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Flag Multiple Row Selection Error When More Than One Row Is Selected
all_rules.Rule_Description: A user is only permitted to select one card row per screen submission. If more than one row has been marked with a View or Update action code, the system flags an error and identifies all offending rows for visual highlighting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to begin the row-by-row evaluation loop for all 7 card list rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row iteration is initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the selected row index (I-SELECTED) to zero, then begins iterating from row 1 through row 7 incrementing by 1 for each iteration

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Selected Row Index Before Row-by-Row Evaluation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before iterating through the 7 card rows to identify which row was selected, the system resets the selected row index to zero to ensure no stale selection index from a prior screen interaction is carried forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is evaluating a specific row (row number I, where I is between 1 and 7) and the row's selection field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(I)) contains either 'S' (View) or 'U' (Update), satisfying the SELECT-OK condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row selection code is evaluated as valid
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current row number (I) into the selected row index variable (I-SELECTED) for later use in navigating to the Card Detail or Card Update screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Selected Row Index for Valid View or Update Selection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a row contains a recognized action code ('S' for View or 'U' for Update), the system records that row's position as the selected row so it can be used to navigate to the appropriate detail or update screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A row contains a valid selection code ('S' or 'U') and the multiple-selection error flag (WS-MORE-THAN-1-ACTION) is TRUE, indicating that more than one row was selected in the same submission
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes that valid-but-conflicting row selection
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the row-level error indicator (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR(I)) to '1' for that specific row, which will cause the selection field to be displayed in red on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Valid Selected Row with Error Indicator When Multiple Selections Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid selection code exists on a row but the multiple-selection error is active (more than one row was selected), the system marks that row with an error indicator so it is highlighted in red on the screen to alert the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is evaluating a specific row (row number I, where I is between 1 and 7) and the row's selection field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(I)) is blank or empty, satisfying the SELECT-BLANK condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row selection code is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system takes no action for that row, does not set any error indicators, does not update I-SELECTED, and continues to the next row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept Blank Row Selection as No Action Requested
all_rules.Rule_Description: A blank selection field on a card row is a valid state indicating the user has not requested any action for that card. No error is raised and the row is simply skipped.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is evaluating a specific row (row number I, where I is between 1 and 7) and the row's selection field (WS-EDIT-SELECT(I)) contains a value that is not 'S', not 'U', and not blank (the OTHER condition in the EVALUATE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row selection code is evaluated as unrecognized
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets INPUT-ERROR to TRUE and sets the row-level error indicator (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR(I)) to '1' for that specific row, which will cause the selection field to be displayed in red on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Flag Invalid Action Code and Mark Row with Error Indicator
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a row's selection field contains a value that is neither a recognized action code ('S' or 'U') nor blank, the system treats it as an invalid action code, marks the row for error highlighting, and sets the overall input error state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An invalid action code has been detected in a row selection field (INPUT-ERROR is TRUE for that row) and the error message slot is currently empty (WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF is TRUE, meaning no prior error message has been set during this validation pass)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to set the invalid action code error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error message (WS-ERROR-MSG) to indicate that an invalid action code was entered by the user (WS-INVALID-ACTION-CODE is set to TRUE, which populates WS-ERROR-MSG with the invalid action code message); if a prior error message already exists (WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF is FALSE), the existing message is preserved and no new message is written

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Invalid Action Code Error Message When No Prior Message Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an invalid action code is detected in a row selection field, the system sets a user-facing error message only if no prior error message has already been set, preserving the first error message encountered during the validation pass.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is accessing the Card List screen either for the first time in a new session (no prior session data exists) OR the user has just navigated from the main menu program into the Card List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Account ID filter field for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips all account filter field value population and attribute setting logic entirely; the account filter field is left in its default initialized state without any value or enterable attribute being explicitly set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Account Filter Display on First Entry or Menu Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is being displayed for the very first time or when the user has navigated from the main menu, the account filter field display logic is bypassed entirely and no filter value population or attribute setting is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a value in the Account ID filter field on the Card List screen AND the entered value has been validated and confirmed as a valid numeric account identifier
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Account ID filter field for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the Account ID filter field on screen with the exact account ID value that was entered by the user (CC-ACCT-ID) AND sets the field attribute to enterable so the user can modify it on the next screen interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Entered Account ID When Filter Is Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account filter value entered by the user has passed numeric validation successfully, the system redisplays the exact value the user typed into the account filter field and makes the field available for editing on the next interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a value in the Account ID filter field on the Card List screen AND the entered value has failed validation because it is not a valid numeric account identifier (filter error state is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Account ID filter field for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the Account ID filter field on screen with the exact invalid account ID value that was entered by the user (CC-ACCT-ID) AND sets the field attribute to enterable so the user can correct the value on the next screen interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retain and Display Entered Account ID When Filter Has Validation Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account filter value entered by the user has failed validation (e.g., non-numeric value), the system still redisplays the invalid value the user typed so they can see and correct it, and keeps the field editable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a value in the Account ID filter field on the Card List screen AND the entered value has failed validation (filter error state is active indicating the account filter is not acceptable)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Account ID filter field display attributes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the Account ID filter field color to red to visually indicate an error AND positions the cursor to the Account ID filter field so the user's attention is directed to the field requiring correction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Account ID Filter Field in Red When Validation Error Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account filter value has failed validation, the system visually highlights the Account ID filter field in red and positions the cursor to it, drawing the user's attention to the field that requires correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Card List screen AND no account ID filter has been applied in the current session, meaning the session-stored account ID value is zero (indicating the user did not supply an account filter)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Account ID filter field for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the Account ID filter field on screen, leaving it blank with no value displayed, so the user sees an empty filter field indicating no account filter is currently active

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Account ID Filter Field When No Account Filter Is Applied
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no account filter has been applied in the current session (the session account ID value is zero, meaning the user left the filter blank or cleared it), the system displays the account filter field as empty/blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Card List screen AND the session contains a previously saved account ID value that is non-zero (a prior account filter was used in a previous interaction) AND the account filter is not currently in a validated or error state from the current submission
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Account ID filter field for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the Account ID filter field on screen with the previously saved session account ID value (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) AND sets the field attribute to enterable so the user can view and optionally modify the previously used account filter value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Previously Saved Account ID From Session When Prior Filter Value Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the session contains a previously saved account ID value that is non-zero and the filter is not in a current validation state, the system restores and displays that saved account ID value in the filter field and makes it editable, allowing the user to see and optionally modify the filter from their prior interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Card List screen and has entered a card number in the card filter field, and the card number filter has been validated successfully (FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the card filter field for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card filter display field (CARDSIDO) is populated with the entered card number value (CC-CARD-NUM), and the card filter field attribute is set to enterable/unprotected (DFHBMFSE) so the user can edit it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Entered Card Number When Card Filter Passes Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number filter entered by the user has passed validation, the card filter display field should show the entered card number value and remain editable so the user can modify it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Card List screen and has entered a card number in the card filter field, and the card number filter has failed validation (FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the card filter field for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card filter display field (CARDSIDO) is populated with the originally entered card number value (CC-CARD-NUM) so the user can see and correct their input, and the card filter field attribute is set to enterable/unprotected (DFHBMFSE) so the user can edit it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Entered Card Number When Card Filter Has a Validation Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number filter entered by the user has failed validation, the card filter display field should still retain and show the originally entered card number value and remain editable so the user can correct it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Card List screen and no card number filter has been entered or saved in the session (CDEMO-CARD-NUM equals zero), and the card filter is neither in a valid nor error state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the card filter field for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card filter display field (CARDSIDO) is cleared to LOW-VALUES (blank), leaving the field empty with no card number displayed and no enterable attribute set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Card Number Filter Field When No Card Number Exists in Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no card number has been stored in the current session (session card number is zero), the card filter display field should be cleared and left blank, indicating no active card filter is in effect.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Card List screen and a card number is stored in the session (CDEMO-CARD-NUM is non-zero), and the card filter state does not match valid (FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID), error (FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK), or zero session card number conditions
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the card filter field for screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card filter display field (CARDSIDO) is populated with the session-stored card number value (CDEMO-CARD-NUM), and the card filter field attribute is set to enterable/unprotected (DFHBMFSE) so the user can edit it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Session Card Number in Filter Field When Card Number Exists in Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card number exists in the session (non-zero) but the filter is not in a specific valid or error state, the card filter display field should show the session-stored card number and remain editable so the user can modify or clear it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card row is displayed on the Card List screen and the user has entered a value in the row's selection field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the entered selection code for row I during input validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the entered code matches a valid action code — 'S' for View or 'U' for Update — the row is treated as a valid selection and proceeds to be recorded as the selected row; otherwise the system checks whether the field is blank or contains an unrecognized code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Valid Row Selection Action Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each card row displayed on the Card List screen, the system evaluates whether the user-entered selection code represents a recognized action. Only 'S' (View card detail) and 'U' (Update card) are valid action codes. This determination drives all subsequent row-level processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card row on the Card List screen contains a valid selection code of 'S' (View) or 'U' (Update)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system validates the row selection during input processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current row number (I) as the selected row index (I-SELECTED), making the account number and card number of that row available for subsequent navigation to the Card Detail or Card Update screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record the Selected Card Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a valid action code ('S' or 'U') in a card row's selection field, the system records the row index as the currently selected row. This selected row index is later used to retrieve the corresponding account number and card number for navigation to the Card Detail or Card Update screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card row contains a valid selection code of 'S' or 'U', and the system has detected that more than one row was selected in the current submission (Multiple Selection Error is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the valid selection code for row I
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system applies an error indicator ('1') to the row's selection error flag (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR for row I), causing the selection field to be highlighted in red on the screen to indicate the multiple-selection violation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Error Indicator to Valid Selection When Multiple Selections Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: Even when a row contains a valid action code ('S' or 'U'), if the system has already detected that more than one row was selected in the same submission, the valid row must also be flagged with an error indicator. This enforces the single-selection-per-submission policy by visually highlighting all selected rows in red, including those with individually valid codes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card row contains a valid selection code of 'S' (View) or 'U' (Update), and no multiple-selection error is active for the current submission
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes validation of the row selection code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row is accepted as a valid single selection with no error indicator applied, the row index is retained as the selected row, and the system proceeds without setting any error condition for this row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Allow Valid Single Selection to Proceed Without Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card row contains a valid action code ('S' or 'U') and no multiple-selection error has been detected, the row is accepted as a clean, valid selection. No error indicator is applied, and the selection is available for use in navigating to the Card Detail or Card Update screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card row is displayed on the Card List screen and the user has left the row's selection field blank (empty, spaces, or low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection code for that row during input validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips the row without recording it as a selected row, without applying any error indicator, and without setting any error message — processing continues to the next row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Blank Row Selection — No Action Required
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user leaves a card row's selection field completely blank (spaces or low-values), it means the user has made no selection for that row. The system treats this as a deliberate non-selection and skips the row entirely without raising any error or recording it as a selected row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card row on the Card List screen contains a selection field value that is not 'S', not 'U', and not blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection code for that row during input validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the overall input status to error (INPUT-ERROR), applies an error indicator ('1') to the row's selection error flag (WS-ROW-CRDSELECT-ERROR for row I) causing the selection field to be highlighted in red, and proceeds to check whether an error message needs to be set

all_rules.Rule_Name: Flag Unrecognized Selection Code as Input Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a value in a card row's selection field that is neither a valid action code ('S' or 'U') nor blank, the system treats it as an invalid input. The overall input is flagged as being in error, and the specific row is marked with an error indicator so it can be highlighted in red on the screen to draw the user's attention.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card row has been identified as containing an unrecognized selection code (not 'S', 'U', or blank), and the system is determining whether to set an error message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether an error message has already been set during the current input validation pass (WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF flag is active, meaning no prior message exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If no prior error message exists, the system sets the error message to indicate an invalid action code was entered (WS-INVALID-ACTION-CODE); if an error message was already set by a prior validation rule (account filter or card filter error), the existing message is preserved and no new message is written

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Invalid Action Code Error Message on First Occurrence
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unrecognized selection code is detected in a card row, the system must display an error message to inform the user. However, to preserve the first error message encountered during validation (error message priority rule), the system only sets the 'Invalid Action Code' message if no prior error message has already been established during the current validation pass.

description:
COCRDLIC is an online CICS program that lists credit cards for a given user. It displays up to 7 credit card records per screen, allowing users to filter by account ID or card number, navigate through pages (forward and backward), and select a card record to either view its details or update it by transferring control to the appropriate downstream program. Admin users can view all cards, while non-admin users see only cards associated with their account in the communication area.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM (CICS File) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Initialize working storage, communication areas, and set default values when the program starts fresh with no prior context (EIBCALEN = 0), setting up transaction ID, program name, user type, and first page indicators. 2: Communication Area Restoration - Restore previously saved session context (commarea) when returning to this program, including last card key, first card key, screen number, and pagination state. 3: Fresh Start Detection - Detect when the user is entering this program from another program (e.g., main menu) and reset all pagination and context data to start a new credit card listing session from the beginning. 4: Function Key Validation - Validate the pressed function key against the set of allowed keys (Enter, PF3, PF7, PF8) and default to Enter key action if an unrecognized key is pressed. 5: Exit to Main Menu - When user presses PF3, transfer control back to the main menu program (COMEN01C), passing the current communication area with updated program context. 6: Pagination State Reset - Reset the 'last page displayed' indicator whenever the user is not pressing PF8 (Page Down), ensuring accurate page tracking for forward/backward navigation. 7: Input Error Handling with Re-display - When input validation errors exist, set up error messages on the screen, attempt to read forward if account and card filters are valid, and re-display the screen with error indicators. 8: Page Up at First Page - When user presses PF7 (Page Up) but is already on the first page, re-read forward from the first card key and redisplay the same first page of results. 9: Page Down Navigation - When user presses PF8 (Page Down) and a next page exists, advance the screen number, read the next set of card records starting from the last card key of the current page, and display the next page. 10: Page Up Navigation - When user presses PF7 (Page Up) and not on the first page, decrement the screen number, read backwards from the first card key of the current page to retrieve the previous page of records, and display it. 11: Transfer to Card Detail View - When user selects a card row with action code 'S' (view) and presses Enter, transfer control to the Card Detail program (COCRDSLC) passing the selected account ID and card number in the communication area. 12: Transfer to Card Update - When user selects a card row with action code 'U' (update) and presses Enter, transfer control to the Card Update program (COCRDUPC) passing the selected account ID and card number in the communication area. 13: Default Forward Read and Display - For all other conditions (initial display, re-entry, etc.), read forward from the first card key and display the current page of credit card records. 14: Screen Header Initialization - Populate screen header fields including application titles, transaction ID, program name, current date (MM/DD/YY format), current time (HH:MM:SS format), and current page number. 15: Screen Data Array Population - Populate up to 7 rows of credit card data on the screen, each row containing the selection indicator, account number, card number, and card active status, skipping rows with no data. 16: Screen Row Attribute Setup - Set display attributes for each of the 7 card selection rows: protect the field if the row is empty or rows are protected due to errors; highlight in red and mark with error indicator if the row has a selection error; otherwise make the field enterable. 17: Search Filter Display Setup - Populate the account ID and card number search filter fields on the screen with current filter values, and position the cursor appropriately based on validation state (error fields highlighted in red, cursor placed at account ID field when no errors). 18: Informational and Error Message Setup - Determine and set the appropriate message to display: 'no previous pages' when PF7 on first page, 'no more pages' when PF8 on last page already shown, action instructions ('TYPE S FOR DETAIL, U TO UPDATE') when records are available, or clear message when appropriate. 19: Screen Transmission - Send the fully populated credit card list screen to the user's terminal, erasing the previous screen content and freeing the keyboard. 20: Screen Input Reception - Receive user input from the credit card list screen, capturing the account ID filter, card number filter, and all 7 row selection indicators entered by the user. 21: Account Filter Validation - Validate the account ID search filter: treat blank/zero values as 'no filter applied'; reject non-numeric values with an error message requiring an 11-digit numeric account number; accept valid numeric values as the active account filter. 22: Card Number Filter Validation - Validate the card number search filter: treat blank/zero values as 'no filter applied'; reject non-numeric values with an error message requiring a 16-digit numeric card number; accept valid numeric values as the active card filter. 23: Row Selection Validation - Validate the selection codes entered in the 7 card rows: count total selections made; reject if more than one row is selected simultaneously with error message; reject invalid action codes (not 'S' or 'U') with error indicator; identify the single selected row index for subsequent action. 24: Forward Card Record Reading - Browse the card file forward from a starting card number key, reading up to 7 records per page, applying account and card filters, storing card number, account ID, and active status for each qualifying record, tracking first and last card keys for pagination, and detecting end-of-file to set next-page indicator. 25: Next Page Existence Check - After filling a full page of 7 records, perform an additional read to determine if more records exist beyond the current page, updating the last card key and next-page indicator accordingly. 26: Backward Card Record Reading - Browse the card file in reverse from the current first card key to retrieve the previous page of records, filling the screen array from bottom to top with up to 7 qualifying records, and updating the first card key for the newly displayed page. 27: Record Filter Application - For each card record read during browsing, apply active filters: if an account filter is set, exclude records where the card's account ID does not match; if a card number filter is set, exclude records where the card number does not match; include the record only if it passes all active filters. 28: Session State Persistence - Before returning control to CICS, save the current program's communication area (including card keys, screen number, pagination indicators, and return flags) combined with the application-wide commarea, so state is preserved across screen interactions. 29: No Records Found Notification - When a forward read on the first page returns zero qualifying records, set the 'no records found' message to inform the user that no credit cards match the current search criteria.
